# Uncertain outcomes, retries, and remote effects

Status: research draft for review, revision 0.2-draft, 2026-10-15. Atlas synthesis by Tamir (Phi Vuong Tuong Tam), with Codex AI assistance. Sources establish protocol facts; the design rules below are Atlas proposals requiring a project's service contract.

## When to load this chapter

Use this chapter when an interaction can create a remote or asynchronous effect: submitting a service request, saving a shared object, handing work to another system, or stopping an agent run. A purely local form does not need this machinery. Combine it with [forms and navigation](forms-and-navigation.md) for the interaction and [state and recovery](state-and-recovery.md#ownership-and-lifetime) for local retention. A locally retained draft or attempt record cannot establish a remote outcome.

## Standard facts and their limits

**Normative HTTP facts.** Safe methods have essentially read-only requested semantics; incidental effects remain possible. Idempotency concerns the intended effect of repeated identical requests, rather than one execution or identical responses. RFC 9110 defines PUT, DELETE, and safe methods as idempotent; non-idempotent automatic retries require knowledge of idempotent semantics or non-application. [RFC 9110 §§9.2.1–9.2.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-9.2.1)

202 means accepted for processing, with completion unsettled; a status monitor is recommended. 200, 201, and 204 describe request success under their respective semantics. [RFC 9110 §§15.3.1–15.3.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-15.3.3)

If-Match uses strong entity-tag comparison to condition an action; false conditions prevent application, with defined response exceptions for already-succeeded changes. 412 concerns failed request preconditions; 409 concerns conflicting resource state. Retry-After provides a follow-up delay, expressed as a date or seconds. [RFC 9110 §13.1.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-13.1.1), [§15.5.10](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-15.5.10), [§15.5.13](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-15.5.13), [§10.2.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-10.2.3)

**Normative browser behavior.** Fetch rejects on network error. Aborting a fetch rejects its unsettled promise and cancels/errors relevant body streams; an already-fulfilled promise stays fulfilled. [WHATWG Fetch §5.6, inspected commit e9460d1](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/e9460d1b22ead1c6a72eeac37fb2ec0dc01aeb1d/#fetch-method)

**Atlas interpretation.** None of these observations alone supplies a whole application's guarantees. A method name does not verify that a service implements the expected behavior. Request success may concern an operation record while downstream work remains pending. Idempotent effect is not universal exactly-once execution. Treat rollback, duplicate prevention, terminal evidence, and retry permission as separate contract questions. A timeout, disconnected stream, or local abort supplies no proof that the service reversed work.

## Outcome states and copy

**Atlas proposal:** represent what is known about the action separately from connection freshness, local waiting, and available controls. These are evidence labels, not a mandatory single linear sequence. Requested can move directly to confirmed or rejected; accepted work can later be rejected; unknown can resolve through lookup. Partial effects need an explicit summary rather than a misleading all-or-nothing label.

| State | Evidence required | Example copy and next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Requested | User intent and action identity recorded locally; delivery unproven | “Submission requested.” Show the intended action. |
| Pending | A matching attempt is awaiting authoritative outcome | “Waiting for submission status.” Keep relevant controls available. |
| Accepted | Service acknowledges receipt or scheduling for the matching action | “Received; processing is pending.” Offer a supported status view. |
| Confirmed | Contract-defined final evidence identifies the actual effect | “Request submitted. Reference R…” Link the resulting record. |
| Rejected | Authoritative refusal/failure identifies this action and its scope | “Submission was declined: …” Explain correction or review. |
| Unknown | Available evidence cannot establish the outcome | “We could not confirm submission. Check status before submitting again.” |

Use “failed” only with a stated scope. A status lookup can fail while an accepted operation continues. Do not replace confirmed historical effects with a generic error because a later refresh fails. An unknown outcome remains visible after a toast disappears, alongside its reference, last checked time, and supported next step. Copy must distinguish “nothing applied” from “some steps applied” whenever the service can establish that difference.

## Service-contract worksheet

Complete this worksheet in the project's design document before promising recovery. Record an owner, documentation or contract revision, and verification evidence for every answer. “Unknown” and “unsupported” are valid answers; they constrain the interface.

Gate promises explicitly: unsupported lookup prevents a promise of reload confirmation; unknown duplicate protection prevents automatic retry after an ambiguous outcome; unsupported cancellation prevents a remote-stop promise. If revision checking is unavailable, record the concurrency limitation and reconciliation route before proposing shared editing. A polished pending indicator cannot fill a missing service capability.

| Contract question | Project decision to record |
| --- | --- |
| What is the effect? | Exact target, actor/account scope, side effects, and whether work spans multiple steps or services. |
| What identifies intent? | Stable action ID; separate proposal ID and proposal version when approval is involved; resource revision used for the decision. |
| What identifies an attempt? | Correlation of each transport attempt with the same action; service operation ID when issued. |
| What prevents duplicates? | Service-enforced mechanism, key scope, concurrency behavior, and whether downstream effects are included. |
| How long is protection retained? | Retention start, expiry, reuse behavior after expiry, and operation-history lifetime. |
| What happens if payload changes? | Which fields define equality, mismatch rejection behavior, and whether a changed intent requires a new action. |
| What proves a terminal result? | Authoritative source, terminal states, effect reference, partial-effect explanation, and freshness/version rules. |
| How is status recovered? | Lookup by action/operation ID, permissions, consistency lag, retention, and meanings of missing or expired records. |
| How is observation paced? | Local wait threshold, poll/push/reconnect policy, server-directed delay, stale/last-observed presentation, stop-waiting and reconciliation escalation. Elapsed time alone proves no remote failure. |
| What may be retried? | Eligible errors, same-action conditions, limits, delay/backoff policy, and the point requiring human reconciliation. |
| What does cancellation mean? | Request scope, acknowledgement versus confirmed stop, race with completion, reversibility, and unsupported cases. |

Stable identity joins a user's reviewed intent to subsequent evidence. Keep the action identity across retries of that same intent, according to the contract; record a new attempt separately. A new key generated on every click defeats a mechanism that recognizes retries by key. Conversely, reusing one key for a changed target or payload can conceal a new intent or produce a conflict. An idempotency key is a contract mechanism, not a guarantee created by naming a header.

A proposal version identifies what the user approved. A resource revision identifies the state that action expected. Neither substitutes for the other or for duplicate prevention. If a proposal changes, require review of the changed proposal before executing it. Avoid storing unnecessary sensitive payloads merely to preserve correlation; specify a minimal, authorized recovery record and its lifetime.

## Dispatch and changed intent

**Atlas proposal:** preserve the immutable submitted snapshot and its action identity separately from the editable draft. Editing creates proposed new intent; it does not alter, cancel or resolve an unresolved action. Before enabling a new action, determine whether its consequence overlaps the unresolved one. Reconcile first or use a specifically documented product/service policy with an accurate explanation of possible multiple effects. A fresh key and another review do not prevent both actions from completing. Keep the original reference and outcome visible independently.

When reload-safe outcome recovery is required, establish an acknowledged minimal recovery identity before dispatch, or use documented authorized service discovery that works independently of the lost reply. Apply the [local acknowledgement boundary](state-and-recovery.md#save-snapshots-and-completion) when a browser record supplies that identity. If retention fails and no independent route exists, gate the effect or explicitly choose a reduced capability whose loss/duplication limits are acceptable to the project; do not retain the recovery promise. Also define failure behavior for later action-to-operation-ID mapping updates. A prepared local entry proves neither delivery nor non-delivery; local retention and the remote effect are not one transaction.

## Safe retry and recovery

**Atlas proposal:** choose the next action using evidence, not a generic “Try again” control.

1. Correlate the observation with the action, payload, and attempt. Reject evidence for an unrelated target, account, action, or proposal version. A delayed authoritative reply from an earlier attempt can settle the same action across retries; apply the contract's freshness/ordering rules and prevent stale state regression.
2. Use an authorized status lookup when available. A confirmed result ends recovery; accepted/pending results keep the operation visible. An authoritative rejection is handled according to its documented scope.
3. Interpret missing status according to the contract. Replication delay, expired history, access changes, and “never received” must not share an assumed meaning. If the service cannot distinguish them, keep the outcome unknown.
4. Retry only when the documented semantics establish acceptable repeated effects or establish that the original action was not applied. Check key retention and payload equality before reusing the action. Apply the contract's attempt limit and pacing; a waiting interval does not itself make repetition safe.
5. Otherwise offer status review, a reference to give support, or another documented reconciliation route. If none exists, state that the outcome cannot be confirmed and leave retry unavailable for that action. Do not invent a recovery route.

After reload or reconnect, recover unresolved action identities from the permitted recovery record, reauthorize lookup, and reconcile before enabling a repeat submission. A local “pending” record is a reminder to investigate, not remote truth. If recovery data was never retained or has expired, say what can still be checked. Reopening the form must not silently create a new action from an unresolved submission.

Specify observation separately from effect retry: the local waiting threshold, supported status-check cadence/backoff, reconnect and hidden-page behavior, last-observed time, stale copy, and when to expose a supported reconciliation route. Respect documented server delays. After a local threshold, replace an indefinite active spinner with truthful delayed/unconfirmed feedback and safe controls; time passing cannot establish failure or authorize another effect. If lookup or escalation is unsupported, say so instead of inventing it.

Use a client button guard to prevent accidental rapid activation and explain the pending state. Service duplicate prevention must also handle another tab, device, reconnect, or direct request. An interface cannot promise protection that exists only in one component's memory. Prefer a specific “Check status” control when that action is supported and useful.

## Cancellation and stale evidence

**Atlas proposal:** distinguish three actions: stop waiting locally, request remote cancellation, and reverse a completed effect. Describe the available one before activation. “Stop waiting” may end observation while work continues. “Request cancellation” remains pending until the service establishes its result. Rollback or compensation needs its own scope, authority, outcome, and recovery design.

When completion races with cancellation, retain both command history and the final effect. “Cancellation requested” cannot replace a completed operation with “Canceled.” A confirmed stop can still leave earlier effects; report them. If stopping is unsupported, the control should explain the available alternative instead of simulating success.

Reconcile updates by identity and documented ordering. Ignore an older progress update for the purpose of replacing a newer known state; retain useful evidence for review. Arrival order and client clocks are insufficient when the service supplies no reliable ordering. If two observations contradict each other and cannot be ordered, show the inconsistency and seek authoritative status rather than inventing a final outcome.

For revision conflicts, preserve the user's draft, obtain current authorized state, and explain the conflict before a new decision. Do not automatically overwrite newer work or replay a previously approved action against a changed resource. Apply the contract's concurrency check; a local version counter alone does not protect remote state. See [concurrent edits](state-and-recovery.md#concurrent-edits).

## Feedback and operator attention

Keep outcome text, evidence links, and controls together. Explain why repeat submission is unavailable without removing access to status or other safe actions. Use the [pending-action and available-control guidance](forms-and-navigation.md#pending-actions-and-available-controls) for accessible announcements and ordinary focus preservation, and [validation and error recovery](forms-and-navigation.md#validation-and-error-recovery) for deliberate recovery targets. Routine progress updates should not take focus. A user-initiated navigation, dialog closure, or correction flow needs a defined target and return path.

## Hypothetical cross-domain cases

These cases illustrate decisions to specify; no service behavior is asserted.

- **Submit a service form:** the user sends one request and loses the connection. Retain its action reference, show unknown outcome, and check the service's supported lookup before offering another submission. Preserve editable draft content without presenting it as proof of non-submission.
- **Save a cart handoff:** a shared cart snapshot is sent to another system. “Handoff accepted” concerns that snapshot and version. A later cart edit requires a fresh review; a saved cart or downstream link alone does not prove the intended handoff finished. Payment and provider implementation are outside this chapter.
- **Cancel an agent:** a stop command is acknowledged while execution events disconnect. Display the command as accepted and execution freshness separately. Confirm stopped only from service evidence; disclose known completed effects. If cancellation is unsupported, say so before presenting a stop control.

## Desk-review validation scenarios

Before implementation, walk each scenario through the worksheet, copy, and recovery decision:

- Double activation followed by a second tab: identify both transport attempts, the service's duplicate boundary, and the visible pending state.
- Service applies the action but its reply is lost: find a route to the original result without creating a new intent.
- Request never arrives, versus lookup temporarily missing or history expired: justify every distinction the interface claims.
- Reload after acceptance; later rejection or partial completion: retain references, preserve drafts, and report the actual scope.
- Same action/key with a changed payload, or a retry after retention expires: demonstrate the explicit gate and next review step.
- Edit the draft while an earlier action remains unknown, then request a new overlapping action: preserve both snapshots and show the reconciliation/consequence gate.
- Lose or deny the recovery-record write before dispatch, or fail its operation-ID mapping update: identify the independent recovery route or blocked promise.
- Exceed a local wait threshold or receive repeated missing/stale status: show truthful delayed feedback, bounded observation and no invented retry permission.
- Old progress arrives after confirmation; cancellation races with completion; conflicting resource revision arrives: identify authoritative evidence and avoid silent regression or overwrite.
- Status updates while a keyboard or assistive-technology user reads or edits: specify announcement, focus, persistent evidence, and available controls using the linked forms guidance.

These are proposed desk-review checks. Source inspection does not establish working service behavior, browser behavior in a project, keyboard operation, or assistive-technology support. Implementation and integration evidence remain required before a project can claim those outcomes.

Fielding, Mark Nottingham, and Julian Reschke. Fetch is written by Anne van Kesteren and maintained by WHATWG. They are references, not endorsers of Atlas. # Prepare frontend design

Produce a self-contained project design.md from the brief and available evidence. Respect the user's theme, scope, output mode and project location. Resolve this Atlas repository from the skill's location; do not confuse it with the consuming project.

## Establish the design

Identify users, essential tasks, content, supported contexts and constraints. Separate supplied facts, observations, proposed decisions and missing inputs. For an existing interface, inspect its governing design document and relevant source or supplied rendered evidence before proposing changes. Repeated code literals alone do not establish intended design rules.

Use [the catalog](../../catalog/themes.json) and candidate theme READMEs to assess fit. Read the selected theme's design.md and sources.md. Preserve an explicit selection; explain needed adaptations. Load motion.md or effects.md only for effects actually chosen. Do not select a stack, backend or additional feature merely to fill the document.

## Load only relevant knowledge

Use [the knowledge index](../../knowledge/README.md) as the topic router. Select material for a concrete project decision; an existing, resolved project rule does not need a fresh survey. Read relevant sections, including dependencies and source credits, rather than every chapter or upstream skill family.

For a new design or unresolved UX decisions, use the general UI/UX guide to connect user goals, information structure, journeys, hierarchy and writing to the chosen visual direction. Route stateful editing to state/recovery and forms/navigation, remote effects to uncertain outcomes, accessibility or adaptive questions to their guide, and human-facing agent work to Agent Experience. Do not add agent, commerce, account or remote-action requirements to unrelated projects. Adapters are conditional on a concrete stack need.

## Make the handoff actionable

Use [the project template](../../templates/project-design.md) as an adaptable outline; omit irrelevant sections. Resolve chosen rules into exact values, semantic pairings, content order, labels, component states and end-to-end task transitions. For applicable flows, name state owners, acknowledgement boundaries, interruption/re-entry, failure recovery and the user's next useful action. External capabilities need an identified input/owner and implementation gate, rather than a fictional endpoint or guarantee.

Retain useful theme rules and explain project adaptations. Record open research questions as questions; heuristic reasoning or synthetic examples are not observed user evidence. Include enough detail for implementation to use the project's documents without reopening Atlas. Add companion documents only when they materially help.

## Preserve evidence and credits

Record the used Atlas/theme revision, selected source creators and URLs, applicable terms/notices, and which values or methods were retained or adapted. For an uncommitted Atlas snapshot, identify that limit and relevant file hashes instead of implying HEAD contains the changes. Propagate relevant chapter credits and [adaptation notices](../../references/skill-adaptations.md); full license texts are redistribution records, not required reading on every invocation.

Use existing read records or metadata-only hashing for source identities. Do not reread source content solely to calculate a fingerprint or populate a provenance table.

Separate performed document, rendered, keyboard, assistive-technology and service checks from future checks. A contrast calculation does not validate an interface. Reconcile contradictions in the draft, then deliver in the requested mode; do not automatically invoke a separate review or implement the product.

# Review frontend design

Review the requested artifact or interface against its brief and governing project decisions. This is an opt-in workflow, not a required step for ordinary frontend edits or preparation. Resolve this Atlas repository from the skill's location. A review alone does not authorize changing project files, replacing its theme, or implementing corrections.

## Choose the evidence and scope

Start with the brief, project design.md and supplied evidence. For document review, assess whether decisions are complete and consistent; do not describe a proposed behavior as observed. When source or rendered review is requested, inspect the relevant implementation or page and record what was actually exercised. Missing browser/tool/service access is a coverage limit, not a passing result.

Do not reload the theme catalog or all source libraries for a project that already has a design contract. Use [the knowledge index](../../knowledge/README.md) to load only the chapter/section needed for an actual review question. Open selected theme rules when checking inheritance or a concrete contradiction. Read relevant source credits when propagating methods; do not load the research ledger or every license text by default.

## Trace tasks and test findings

Trace the essential user paths, including relevant empty, invalid, pending, interrupted and recovery states. Consider general UI/UX as part of those tasks: information order, hierarchy, terminology, action labels, type readability, semantic color and responsive/input behavior. Use the accessibility/responsive guide for implicated components or contexts. For stateful or asynchronous actions, check the relevant state, forms and uncertain-outcome contracts. Use Agent Experience only when the product exposes agent work or decisions.

For persistent edits, remote effects or changing human-agent proposals, use the [state-transition review profile](references/state-transitions.md) to trace applicable acknowledgement, retirement, re-entry and late-evidence boundaries. Select its relevant traces rather than treating a future-test list as a completed behavior contract.

For each candidate issue, identify the governing requirement or supported usability concern, the exact document/source location or observed state, a reproducible trigger, and the consequence for a user task. Check nearby rules and alternative paths for counterevidence before reporting it. Distinguish a standard requirement, project contract, source heuristic and aesthetic preference. A legitimate theme choice is not a defect merely because another skill prefers a different style.

Prioritize by task impact and recoverability. Consolidate duplicate symptoms under their cause. A documented external dependency may be an open contract rather than a contradiction; flag an unsupported promise or an ungated dependent action. Keep unknown service behavior unknown. Do not use invented participants, synthetic personas, a numerical design score or source inspection as proof of usability, accessibility conformance or successful execution.

## Deliver the review

Report actionable findings first. Each needs severity/reason, precise location, trigger and consequence, evidence, and a bounded suggested correction. Record unresolved inputs with an owner or required evidence when known. If there are no actionable findings, say so and describe the meaningful checks and remaining limits.

Include a short coverage record: material read, task/state paths inspected, appearances and viewport/input contexts checked when applicable, and checks not performed. Separate document, source, browser, keyboard, assistive-technology and real-service evidence. Suggest fixes without applying them unless the user separately authorizes implementation. Do not automatically run preparation or a second full audit.

Preserve the project's existing credits and distinguish Atlas recommendations from upstream material. Method credits and license notices are in [skill adaptations](../../references/skill-adaptations.md); propagate relevant attribution with any distributed substantial adaptation.

# Review state-transition boundaries

Use for persistent editing, consequential remote actions or human-agent decisions. Choose applicable traces; do not add those capabilities to a static surface. These are original Atlas review questions grounded in the existing P0 chapters, not new platform or service guarantees.

Trace a concrete candidate through its draft, queued work, acknowledgement, current authority and next user action. Read the governing project rules first; use the linked sections to resolve a specific question. Check both the declared behavior and every path that can bypass its boundary.

| When applicable | Trace to reconcile in the document | Selective reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A save can overlap newer editing | An old candidate completes after a newer draft exists: which exact candidate becomes acknowledged, which editing remains dirty, and can a create become a duplicate rather than an update? | [Save snapshots](../../../knowledge/state-and-recovery.md#save-snapshots-and-completion) |
| Work is discarded, removed, finalized or replaced while writes remain queued | The destructive change succeeds, then obsolete work arrives. What makes every writer reject the retired draft/object identity or generation? A deletion acknowledgement alone does not retire an old writer. What is retained if retirement fails? | [Replacement and stale writers](../../../knowledge/state-and-recovery.md#replacement-and-stale-writers), [dirty exit](../../../knowledge/forms-and-navigation.md#modal-editing-and-dirty-exit) |
| A remote request or retry can outlive its screen | The effect may occur without a reply, then the user returns or changes intent. How is the original action found, and what gates a new or repeated effect? | [Dispatch and changed intent](../../../knowledge/uncertain-outcomes.md#dispatch-and-changed-intent), [safe recovery](../../../knowledge/uncertain-outcomes.md#safe-retry-and-recovery) |
| Observations or attempts may arrive late | An older matching observation arrives after a newer result, or observations contradict. What identity/payload and service-defined ordering can qualify evidence? What preserves confirmed history and exposes a contradiction when ordering is unavailable? A failed refresh rule alone does not settle late successful responses. | [Cancellation and stale evidence](../../../knowledge/uncertain-outcomes.md#cancellation-and-stale-evidence) |
| A person reviews a changing proposal | Scope or target changes before application. Which reviewed version is authorized, what revalidates it at execution, and what must be reviewed again? | [Agent control questions](../../../knowledge/agent-experience.md#resolve-project-control-questions) |

A future-test list names work still to do; it does not supply the behavior an implementer needs. Distinguish an explicit capability gate with an owner from an omitted local decision or an unconditional promise behind that gate. Do not invent ordering, atomicity, retention or cancellation support. Report a bounded missing rule only when the trace exposes a material task or recovery consequence; an alternative coherent design can close it.

For every finding, try the strongest counterexample in the document before reporting it. Keep proposed fixes separate from the unmodified review input. Source/method credits and retained notices remain in [the adaptation record](../../../references/skill-adaptations.md).

# Blueprint

Cobalt lines, cool paper, technical type, small corners, and restrained offset shadows establish a drafting character. A faint grid supports selected visual studies; clear headings and ordinary page structure carry the content. The direction remains recognizable without a moving wireframe or cursor effect.

This entry adapts Blueprint in **Tamir (Phi Vuong Tuong Tam)'s portfolio**, retaining observed values and identifying portable Atlas proposals. The source pairs Manrope interface text with JetBrains Mono accents and technical values. Atlas proposes a broader mono heading role while keeping body text and controls in sans-serif. Its original preview applies the direction to a fictional engineering studio and an architecture inspector.

## Suitability

These are Atlas assessments, not measured usability results.

| Project type | Fit | Reason and adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engineering studio | Strong | Technical type and measured composition suit systems work and process descriptions. Distinguish diagrams, proposals, and built outcomes. |
| Developer documentation | Strong | Mono identifiers and quiet navigation support technical reference. Keep reading text in sans-serif and verify code scrolling and language coverage. |
| Systems portfolio | Strong | A drafting identity can connect problem statements, architecture, decisions, and contributions. Use real evidence in production case studies. |
| Technical product | Strong | Explicit labels and ordered detail support explanation and inspection. Blue styling alone does not establish authority or correctness. |
| Architecture explorer | Strong | Diagram nodes can be paired with a keyboard-accessible outline and readable details. Preserve an equivalent text description of relationships. |
| Agent operations | Conditional | Needs separate authority, execution, pending-command, error, connection, and recovery rules. A technical diagram is not an operational control surface. |
| Long-form publication or lifestyle brand | Conditional | Retain a comfortable reading measure and reserve mono/grid treatments for short emphasis. A softer display treatment may better fit narrative identity. |

Choose the adaptation for actual content and tasks. A visual direction does not establish agent permissions, execution, or recovery behavior. Use relevant [Agent Experience guidance](../../knowledge/agent-experience.md) when preparing an agent interface.

## Spacing and layout

**Proposed scale:** 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, and 96px.

- Label to control: 8px; related controls: 12px.
- Related content groups: 16–24px; major sections: 48–96px.
- Comfortable panel inset: 24px; compact specimen inset: 16px.
- Typical content maximum: 1120px; reading maximum: 65ch.
- Proposed gutters: 24px on small screens and 40px when room permits; adapt narrower screens to actual content fit.

Start with one column. Add columns when the actual labels and content fit, preserving DOM reading order. The source shared hero becomes two columns from 1024px; this observation is not a universal project breakpoint.

An architecture diagram is one representation of relationships, not the sole route to understanding them. Provide a readable outline and explicit relationship text. Use the same node collection and selection state across presentations. Keep nodes as native links or buttons; a fixed collection with no tree keyboard contract should not use tree roles.

The preview's comfortable studio and architecture workspace remain independent of density. Compact changes **only the neutral component specimen's inset from 24px to 16px**; typography, control targets, 8px/4px corners, and inspector layout retain their values. A project needing a broader compact profile records its separate adaptations.

Preserve long titles, names, and identifiers. A semantic relationship table that requires horizontal room belongs in a labeled keyboard-accessible scrolling region, while the whole page reflows. Recheck content order and focus at narrow widths and with enlarged text.

# Blueprint — optional effects

The core identity comes from cobalt color, technical hierarchy, small corners, and ordered composition. Projects deliberately select decoration. [Design rules](design.md) define readable content; [motion rules](motion.md) define immediate fallbacks.

## Static drafting motifs

**Source:** selected hero and specimen regions use a 24px grid, drawn with `#1644b80b` lines in light appearance and `#8ab7ff12` in dark. Project boundaries, profile outlines, and orbit lines can be dashed. Resting panels use 8px corners, controls 4px corners, and a small low-alpha offset shadow.

These are decorative treatments. Faint grids, dashed construction lines, and offset shadows do not replace a necessary control boundary, a diagram relationship, or a selected-state label. Do not place a faint background grid beneath every paragraph or dense table.

**Atlas proposal:** use a bounded static study with plain content separate from it. Original preview vector art and architecture diagrams are Atlas compositions; neither is exported portfolio artwork or an external component implementation. Diagram relationships that convey meaning require readable labels and an equivalent text account, independently of decorative geometry.

## Projected wireframe

**Source concept:** Tamir's portfolio has an original Canvas 2D scene inspired by **Meng To / ThreeUI's [Wireframe Forms](https://21st.dev/@mengto/components/wireframe-forms/wireframe-forms-cylinders)**. Projected linework follows the pointer; an explicit action cycles cube, sphere, and cylinders. The [ThreeUI reference](https://threeui.com/ui-elements/wireframe-forms) separately describes rotating Canvas 2D forms.

**Atlas proposal:** disabled by default. A project may select one bounded hero study with an explicit native action. Keep core headings, navigation, descriptions, and controls in HTML, usable if artwork fails.

- Mark pure decoration `aria-hidden`; prevent it intercepting pointer input or keyboard navigation.
- Keep effect activation separate from navigation and meaningful diagram inspection. Label the effect control by its actual action.
- Use static composition for coarse pointers, reduced motion, and motion-off. Avoid reading regions, repeated review work, logs, or changing operational values.
- If adopting source eligibility, defer the renderer to hover-capable, fine-pointer desktops at least 1024px wide; cap pixel density at 2 and pause offscreen and in hidden tabs.
- Remove frames, observers, and resize/pointer/visibility listeners when replacing the effect.
- Recheck composited text and focus contrast across frames. Opaque token calculations do not validate translucent artwork.

**Source character:** a 32px circular supplementary mark with a faint outline and 42px horizontal/vertical axes, following the pointer in the current accent color. The native pointer remains intact, the follower does not receive events, and source logic hides it during keyboard/text-entry interaction and stops idle frames.

# Blueprint — motion specification

Feedback should clarify an interaction while keeping content and targets stable. Inspected source settings and portable Atlas choices are distinct. Pinned files and creator credits are in [sources.md](sources.md).

## Retained source settings

| Role | Source setting | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Theme Motion transition | 300ms tween, `easeInOut` | Separate JavaScript transition setting, not the CSS feedback duration. |

The pinned artwork notes describe the homepage hero as immediately visible after its separate brand introduction, with no entrance animation or stagger. Do not infer active hero behavior from a helper definition. Atlas does not adopt the portfolio loading introduction, animated identity sequence, theme reveal, theme cycling, or tracing as an automatic reading effect.

## Proposed project rules

Use **240ms color and border feedback** with the declared CSS easing uniformly as an Atlas normalization. The reference preview selects this restrained feedback only. Feedback duration is not a simulated operation delay.

Show essential content immediately. A project selecting the 300ms source transition or entrance records its specific purpose; use it once for a secondary region with content already available. Do not replay on appearance changes, filtering, refreshes, or return navigation. An effect called a traced path does not justify delaying the text it illustrates.

Diagram and outline selection, filtering, opening detail, return focus, and announcements happen immediately. Do not move a focused control, animate sorting into a new location, or depend on animation completion to reveal information. Keep selection and content context stable when switching a diagram view.

Compact projects may choose 120–180ms feedback; record that adaptation rather than treating it as an observed Blueprint default. Optional press and hover transforms can be omitted when they reduce repeated-use clarity. The preview contains no entrances, moving cards, cursor effects, animated scrolling, looping artwork, or delayed interaction state.

## Reduced motion and user control

Honor `prefers-reduced-motion` from first paint, with OS reduced motion taking priority over enabled project motion. A visible motion preference can make feedback immediate without changing information.

- Remove transition delays, transforms, and entrance offsets; content stays visible in its final position.
- Keep navigation and focus transfer immediate.
- Replace optional canvas/cursor movement with a static view and stop hidden loops.
- Preserve explicit state labels and announcements without relying on motion.
- Do not animate connectors as evidence of actual traffic, progress, or agent execution unless the product defines and exposes those real states separately.

Test live preference changes, keyboard focus, immediate initial content, and no-JavaScript behavior. Any later renderer needs its own pause, cleanup, performance, and accessibility checks; static reference-preview checks do not validate unimplemented effects.

# Botanical

Earthy greens, warm paper, expressive serif headings, alternating rounded corners, and selective soft shadows give content an organic character. Comfortable spacing supports stories and reading; restrained feedback keeps controls clear. The direction remains recognizable with static artwork and immediate state changes.

This entry adapts Botanical in **Tamir (Phi Vuong Tuong Tam)'s portfolio**, retaining observed values and labeling portable Atlas proposals. Manrope carries body and interface text, DM Serif Display has an expressive heading role, and JetBrains Mono supports short technical values. Atlas's original preview applies the direction to a fictional garden studio and a small reading room.

Page is the base. Use panel and surface for meaningful grouping, and tints sparingly to connect related stories. A heading or section rule can provide structure without a card. Accent supports expressive details; action/on-action is the explicit filled-action pair.

Decorative dividers are gentle rules, not a sufficient sole boundary for every input or control. Use the proposed necessary control border wherever a boundary identifies an actionable region. Verify every adjacent color the boundary or focus indicator crosses.

The warning, danger, and information proposals are **foregrounds** for text/icons on the six page, surface, panel, and tint backgrounds. They do not define filled statuses or buttons. The source selected-item token is used by a component selection layer. Its global text-selection rule separately uses a shared lime token. Applying the Botanical selected-item surface to user text selection is an **Atlas adaptation**, paired with ink. Keep useful text selectable.

Muted text fails ordinary-text contrast in both appearances, dark accent fails ordinary-text contrast, and the proposed dark control border falls below 3:1 there. ## Spacing and layout

**Proposed scale:** 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, and 96px.

- Label to control: 8px; related controls: 12px.
- Related content groups: 16–24px; major sections: 48–96px.
- Comfortable panel padding: 24px; compact specimen padding: 16px.
- Typical site width: up to 1120px; reading width: 65ch.
- Page gutters: 24px on small screens and 40px when room permits; reduce only when a narrow viewport requires it.

Start with one column. Add columns when the actual content fits; preserve DOM reading order as the layout stacks. The source's shared hero uses a one-column title/intro sequence, then a two-column layout from 1024px. That source threshold is an observation, not a universal breakpoint for every project.

The preview's garden studio and reading room remain comfortable. Its density preference changes **only the neutral component specimen's insets** from 24px to 16px. Typography and organic geometry retain their comfortable values. Record any further compact rules in a project's own design document; they are adaptations, not a second source default.

Wrap long titles and identifiers. Keep essential article content in normal flow, with stable list/detail context during filtering. Necessary table overflow belongs in a labeled, keyboard-accessible scrolling region; the whole page should reflow at narrow widths.

Use native controls, landmarks, descriptive headings, a skip link where useful, and a logical keyboard sequence. The proposed comfortable touch target is **44px**; this is a usability target, not a statement of WCAG's minimum. The source's optional desktop project hover translates upward 4px with `0 20px 35px -22px #293d2f55`. It is restricted to hover-capable devices without reduced motion and with motion enabled. Atlas's reference preview selects color/border feedback only; it does not adopt moving cards.

## Living contour concept

**Source behavior:** Tamir's original Canvas 2D adaptation draws organic green contours, responds to the pointer, and sends a bloom outward when activated. Its notes credit **Kedhareswer Naidu / @kedhareswer's [Isoline Bloom](https://21st.dev/@kedhareswer/components/isoline-bloom)** as conceptual inspiration. The local renderer adds no new dependency or WebGL context.

The source defers the artwork to fine-pointer, hover-capable desktops at least 1024px wide. A native labeled button exposes the deliberate response to keyboard users. Reduced motion and motion-off keep artwork static and disable the effect action. Observers stop frames when hidden or offscreen; pixel density is capped at 2; listeners, observers, and frames are cleaned up when the scene is removed.

**Atlas proposal:** static composition by default. A project may let users explicitly enable contours in one presentation region. Keep article reading areas and working surfaces calm, and recheck text after compositing artwork beneath it.

- Keep essential content and controls in normal HTML, readable independently of the drawing.
- Mark pure decoration `aria-hidden` and prevent pointer interception. An intentional response belongs to a separate native labeled control.
- Provide a static treatment on touch/coarse pointers, reduced motion, or motion-off.
- Pause continuous work when hidden/offscreen and clean up frames, observers, and listeners on removal.
- Never use decorative blooming to indicate success, saving, permission, selection, or progress.

No contour implementation is included in this package. The external listing's MIT indication must be checked against the exact future package/version, dependencies, and required notices before importing its code. The portfolio's own implementation terms remain a separate unresolved matter.

**Source character:** a supplementary 28px leaf mark, 1.4 stroke weight, rotated -18 degrees, following a mouse with a time-adjusted smoothing coefficient of 0.14. The native pointer remains available. The source hides the follower for text entry, keyboard interaction, lost window focus, hidden documents, coarse pointers, reduced motion, motion-off, and forced colors. Frames stop when movement settles.

If chosen for a fine-pointer presentation region, retain native pointers and hit targets, prevent event interception, preserve those eligibility rules, and verify that it never obscures reading or focus. A particular leaf icon requires its own selected asset/source record; this package includes no source icon or follower implementation.

# Editorial

Warm paper surfaces, muted lavender, expressive serif accents, rounded geometry, and soft transitions support a content-first interface. The source implementation combines Manrope for readable interface text, DM Serif Display for selected expressive text, and JetBrains Mono for short technical values.

This Atlas entry adapts the Editorial direction in Tamir's portfolio. It distinguishes retained source values from proposed portable rules; it does not include the portfolio's branding, copy, artwork implementation, or font files.

## Suitability

These assessments are Atlas judgments, not measured performance or usability results.

| Project type | Fit | Reason and adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Portfolio or case studies | Strong | Expressive headings and comfortable spacing support storytelling and project evidence. Keep effects optional. |
| Publication or journal | Strong | Warm surfaces and a restrained serif role support long reading. Apply a readable measure and continuous heading hierarchy. |
| Boutique service or product site | Strong | Calm presentation suits a small set of clear offers, product stories, and actions. Preserve explicit action contrast. |
| Agent workspace | Conditional | Retain the palette and readable sans-serif text; adapt density, geometry, typography, and motion for frequent operations. |
| Operations dashboard | Conditional | Use compact controls, stable data layouts, explicit status labels, and restrained update feedback. Decorative scenes are unnecessary. |
| Dense analytics | Conditional | Requires documented data typography, compact geometry, table conventions, and chart/status semantics beyond the source portfolio. |

A project must choose and document its adaptation. A visual theme does not define agent execution, permission, or recovery behavior.

## Package

- [Design specification](design.md): tokens, typography, hierarchy, spacing, components, appearance, and accessibility rules.
- [Motion specification](motion.md): source timings, proposed compact adaptations, and reduced-motion behavior.
- [Optional effects](effects.md): selective shadows, flowing paths, and a cursor halo.
- [Sources and credits](sources.md): source snapshot, creator roles, font notices, inspiration, and adaptation records.

Projects can implement this specification without a theme-specific runtime or animation library.

## Preview and validation

A [live reference preview](https://tamir39.github.io/interface-atlas/themes/editorial/preview/) demonstrates neutral components and representative portfolio and agent operations layouts. Read the [preview notes](preview/README.md) for scope, or open [index.html](preview/index.html) locally for offline use. It has no build or external resource dependency and uses local font fallbacks; named webfont files and optional source artwork are not included.

The [validation report](validation.md) records browser checks and their limits. Numerical token calculations remain in [design.md](design.md). This entry stays a draft: representative preview evidence does not validate every adaptation, font package, assistive technology, browser, or backend integration.

The local Editorial implementation is credited to **Tamir (Phi Vuong Tuong Tam)**. Font designers are **Mikhail Sharanda** for Manrope, **Colophon Foundry** for DM Serif Display, and **JetBrains, Philipp Nurullin, and Konstantin Bulenkov** for JetBrains Mono.

Use page as the base and panels for meaningful groups, rather than placing every element inside a card. Surface supports secondary regions. Accent decorates selected expressive text or details; action and on-action form an explicit foreground/background pair.

Muted text remains readable supporting text. Decorative dividers cannot be the sole boundary identifying an input or control; use the proposed stronger control border where that boundary is necessary.

Warning, danger, and information colors are foregrounds for text and icons on page, surface, or panel. Their values do not define filled badges or buttons. Pair every status with a textual label and, where useful, an icon. Recheck any alternative background, opacity, image, or blend.

Selection indicates user text selection or an explicitly selected item, not an unexplained status. When using the source note treatment, pair note with on-note. When using success as a filled background, pair it with on-success.

## Typography and hierarchy

**Source font families:** Manrope for body text, controls, and most headings; DM Serif Display 400 normal or italic for selected expressive text; JetBrains Mono 400/500 for short code and identifiers.

The source font configuration loads Latin and Vietnamese for Manrope and Latin for the other two families. Verify actual glyph coverage and fallback behavior for each project's languages. Preserve the correct font package notices if font files are redistributed.

**Proposed portable scale:**

| Role | Family and weight | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Display | Manrope 500; optional DM Serif Display 400 accent | `clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem)` | `1.08` |
| Page heading | Manrope 600 or DM Serif Display 400 | `clamp(2rem, 4vw, 3rem)` | `1.15` |
| Section heading | Manrope 600 | `1.5rem` | `1.3` |
| Card heading | Manrope 600 | `1.125rem` | `1.4` |
| Body | Manrope 400 | `1rem` | `1.65` |
| Introduction | Manrope 400 | `1.125rem` | `1.6` |
| Labels and supporting text | Manrope 400–600 | `0.875rem` | `1.5` |

This scale is an Atlas adaptation, not a transcription of every portfolio heading. Moderate display tracking to at most `-0.02em`; keep body tracking normal. Do not apply tightly tracked hero styling to controls or dense data.

Follow semantic heading order and choose sizes by content role. Keep reading passages around 60–70 characters per line. Use tabular numerals for aligned data, durations, and counts. Monospace is a role-specific accent, not the default body typeface.

## Spacing and layout

**Proposed scale:** 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, and 96px.

- Label to control: 8px.
- Related controls: 12px.
- Card groups: 16–24px.
- Major sections: 48–96px, selected according to content density.
- Panel padding: 24px by default; 16px in constrained regions.
- Content width: 1120px maximum for a typical comfortable site.
- Page gutters: 24px on small screens, 40px when room permits.

Start with one column and introduce columns when the content comfortably fits. The DOM reading order must match the intended visual order. Wrap long identifiers or provide explicit full-value access. Place necessary data overflow inside a labeled, discoverable scrolling region rather than allowing the entire page to overflow.

Projects may define a compact adaptation with smaller geometry and spacing for dense workflows. Record those overrides in the project's design document; they are not source defaults.

## Geometry and elevation

**Source:** card radius 24px; control radius 999px.

**Source light shadow:** `0 16px 40px -28px #493b6155`.

**Source dark shadow:** `0 20px 45px -24px #00000099`.

Use the source shadow selectively on meaningful raised panels. Avoid adding shadows to every nested group. A 12px radius for inputs and nested controls is an Atlas proposal for predictable text-entry geometry. Compact card and control radii must be stated as project adaptations.

## Component behavior

| Component | Proposed rule |
| --- | --- |
| Primary action | Use action/on-action; hover uses action-hover with the same foreground. Preserve a visible focus treatment and stable dimensions. |
| Secondary action | Panel or transparent background, primary text, and a sufficiently visible boundary where needed. |
| Prose link | Underline or another persistent non-color cue; keep hover and focus discoverable. |
| Input | Visible associated label, panel background, text token, and proposed control border. |
| Card | Group related content; a card is not automatically an interactive element. |
| Status | Text plus optional icon on a verified neutral background; color supplements meaning. |
| Dialog | Width follows its content and viewport; actions remain visible and focus is managed. |
| Table | Semantic headers, appropriately aligned values, and discoverable contained overflow. |

Define default, hover, focus, pressed or selected, unavailable, and pending states wherever relevant. Use explicit pending labels such as “Saving…” rather than relying on a spinner. Keep geometry stable during pending updates.

Associate field errors with their inputs and place recovery information near the field. Explain unavailable actions visibly when their reason matters. Do not put essential explanations only inside hover tooltips.

## Appearance and accessibility

Support light, dark, and system choices. Apply the saved choice before paint where possible, follow live system changes when system is selected, and preserve essential content if storage or initialization is unavailable.

**Source focus treatment:** 3px outline using the text token, with a 5px offset. Prevent clipping, verify contrast against adjacent surfaces, and use an appropriate system color in forced-colors mode.

Use native controls, landmarks, a skip link where needed, visible labels, and a logical keyboard sequence. Aim for 44px touch areas as an Atlas comfort target; this is not presented as the WCAG minimum. Verify zoom, reflow, keyboard interaction, screen-reader information, and actual AA contrast in the implemented project.

Essential content is visible without motion. Follow [motion.md](motion.md) for animation and [effects.md](effects.md) for optional decoration.

# Editorial — optional effects

A project explicitly selects any effect in this document. Effects do not determine the theme's suitability and are not prerequisites for its identity. Use [design.md](design.md) for the readable content layer and [motion.md](motion.md) for motion controls.

## Selective panel shadow

**Source light:** `0 16px 40px -28px #493b6155`.

**Source dark:** `0 20px 45px -24px #00000099`.

Use this on a meaningful raised panel when elevation helps grouping. Avoid shadows on every card inside an already raised panel. Maintain a visible boundary when the shadow does not provide adequate separation.

## Flowing paths

**Source behavior:** Tamir's portfolio includes an original Canvas 2D adaptation of the flowing-path interaction concept, credited locally to **Bundui.io's [Floating Paths](https://21st.dev/@bundui/components/floating-paths)**. Fine lavender paths flow slowly, bend toward the pointer, and respond to a click with a wave.

The local artwork notes explicitly describe custom adaptations rather than imported catalog source code. The external component's implementation reuse permission has not been established; do not treat the inspiration credit as permission to copy it.

**Atlas proposal:** default to a static treatment. A project may offer an explicit control to enable motion in one hero region. Avoid article reading areas, data tables, logs, and operational workspaces.

- Keep essential text and controls in normal HTML and readable independently of the canvas.
- Mark purely decorative artwork `aria-hidden`; it must not intercept pointer or keyboard interaction.
- If an effect has an intentional interactive action, expose it through a separate native labeled control. Pure decoration does not create a hidden page action.
- Use a static treatment for touch, coarse pointers, reduced motion, and motion-off.
- Retain the source implementation's deferred desktop eligibility, pixel-density cap of 2, and hidden/offscreen pausing where a project adopts this behavior.
- Clean up animation frames and resize, visibility, and pointer listeners when the effect is removed or replaced.

The implementation code is not included in this package. A separate implementation or authorized adaptation would require its own source and reuse record.

## Cursor halo

**Source character:** an optional 32px circle, an accent outline, and a 6% tinted fill. It is supplementary to the native pointer.

**Atlas proposal:** disabled by default. If selected for a fine-pointer interface, retain the native pointer, prevent event interception, hide around text-entry and keyboard interaction, and disable on coarse pointers, reduced motion, or motion-off. Stop animation frames when the follower settles.

Do not use the halo to communicate selection, permission, progress, or control availability.

## Acceptance checks

Verify text contrast after compositing, focus visibility, native-pointer behavior, keyboard access, touch fallback, reduced motion, explicit motion controls, hidden/offscreen animation pausing, and frame cleanup.

A failed effect must leave content and controls usable. A static fallback must not change reading order or replace essential information.

Source creator, source snapshot, conceptual inspiration, and reuse status are recorded in [sources.md](sources.md).

# Editorial — motion specification

Motion should clarify a change while keeping content and controls available. The timings below distinguish inspected source settings from Atlas proposals. See [sources.md](sources.md) for pinned source links and credits.

## Retained source settings

| Role | Source setting | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSS component feedback | 240ms; declared `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | The inspected transition shorthand applies the theme easing explicitly to transform. Applying it uniformly to every feedback property is an Atlas normalization. |
| Theme entrance | 380ms tween, `easeOut` | Initial opacity 0 and vertical offset 12px; final opacity 1 and offset 0. |
| Press response | Scale `0.96` | Optional source interaction, not required for all controls. |

The source CSS feedback and entrance timings serve different roles. Do not collapse them into a single universal duration.

## Proposed project rules

Keep essential hero and page content visible immediately. A secondary section may reveal once when it becomes relevant. Avoid replaying entrances when a theme changes, data refreshes, or the operator returns through navigation.

Animate the component that changes. Do not move focused controls, reflow a live list, or stagger important content by default. Do not introduce typewriter text as a default reading behavior.

For compact operational interfaces, proposed alternatives are:

- 150ms feedback for a control state change.
- 180ms opacity transition for a panel.
- No entrance movement during streamed data updates.

These compact timings are Atlas additions, not retained portfolio values. A project selects and records them explicitly.

The optional press scale may be disabled where movement interferes with frequent interaction, pointer accuracy, or data review. It must not be the sole indication that an action was accepted.

## Reduced motion and user control

Honor either an OS reduced-motion preference or a project's motion-off setting. Use immediate state changes, remove entrance offsets and scales, disable loops, and replace animated scrolling with immediate movement. Preserve visible feedback, state text, and data updates.

Atlas intentionally uses an immediate reduced-motion policy rather than retaining optional opacity animation. No workflow, control availability, loading completion, or focus transfer may depend on an animation completion event.

Continuous decoration requires an explicit user control. Pause animation when the page is hidden or the affected region is offscreen. The off state must persist for the selected preference scope.

## Verification

Check reduced motion at first paint and after a live preference change, project motion-off behavior, keyboard focus stability, repeated navigation, and interrupted animations. Confirm that content remains available if the animation runtime fails.

# Gallery

Imagery determines the composition. Quiet sans-serif typography, generous whitespace, unboxed media, small off-image captions, flat surfaces, and near-square controls let a collection establish its own character. A restrained neutral interface supports both complete-object inspection and deliberate contextual crops.

Gallery is an **original Interface Atlas synthesis for Tamir (Phi Vuong Tuong Tam), with Codex AI assistance**. Shopify's design documentation and Dawn/Horizon listings inform image-led presentation and content resilience; web.dev, W3C WAI, and web standards inform image delivery and interaction. No referenced theme implementation is adapted or imported. Every numerical value, layout, crop policy, artwork, and workflow is an Atlas proposal.

This direction differs from Editorial's reading-led serif composition, Swiss's structural rules, and Botanical's organic geometry. Gallery makes the media system itself a first-class design decision: what can be cropped, what must remain complete, how captions behave, and what survives unavailable imagery.

## Suitability

These are Atlas assessments, not measured usability, conversion, or performance results.

| Project type | Fit | Reason and adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image portfolio | Strong | Work can lead the composition while names, roles, and evidence remain ordinary text. Record real image credits and permissions. |
| Collection or exhibition site | Strong | Consistent captions and deliberate ratios connect varied pieces without flattening their differences. Add indexing appropriate to the collection. |
| Design catalog or lookbook | Strong | Large media and quiet metadata support visual comparison. Keep object accuracy separate from contextual crops. |
| Architecture or interiors site | Strong | Wide views and detail images can form a coherent account of space. Each image needs its own creator and rights record. |
| Boutique storefront | Conditional | The visual direction suits image-heavy discovery. Variants, prices, stock, cart, and checkout need researched project flows; they are not supplied by this theme. |
| Publication | Conditional | Use image-led essays and captions, then add the reading, navigation, and media-credit conventions needed for long content. |
| Agent workspace or dense analytics | Strained | Large media and comfortable presentation provide little advantage for frequent operational tasks. Additional data, density, authority, and recovery rules are required. |

A theme supplies visual language rather than a complete product model. A project records its selected adaptation and relevant [Agent Experience decisions](../../knowledge/agent-experience.md) when those apply.

Use page for the main canvas and panel/surface only where grouping is useful. Media and its caption can stand directly on the page. The warm accent supports deliberate actions; imagery supplies most of the composition's color. Avoid turning every work into an elevated card.

Action/on-action and hover/on-action are defined pairs. Success, warning, danger, and information are **foreground roles**, not filled backgrounds with inferred text colors. ## Spacing, layout, and geometry

**Proposed spacing scale:** 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, and 96px. Label-to-control spacing starts at 8px, related controls at 12px, caption groups at 8–12px, and major sections at 48–96px. A portable content maximum is **1280px**, with 16px narrow gutters and 32px when room permits; consuming projects document content-fit changes.

**Media corners: 0px. Panels: 4px. Controls: 4px.** Surfaces rest flat without shadows. Comfortable is the default. Compact changes only the **neutral component specimen's inset from 24px to 16px**; it does not shrink collection imagery, captions, the inline viewer, body type, or target size.

Start with one column and add columns when real media and captions fit. Image scale and alternating visual weight may create asymmetry, but the DOM reading order stays useful. Do not apply masonry or CSS ordering that disconnects visual order from keyboard or reading order. Repeated cards use a stable scan pattern for image, name, category/context, and Inspect action.

Use whitespace, scale, and image relationships as the primary structure. A rule, colored panel, rounded badge, or serif heading should not become the whole identity. Keep a coherent caption baseline where repeated cards need comparison; long names may take more lines without clipping or hiding the action.

Contain a semantic table's genuine overflow in a labeled, keyboard-focusable scrolling region. The page itself must reflow. Long identifiers, Vietnamese content, enlarged text, and changed font metrics remain useful without losing essential information.

The preview deliberately selects a wider **1440px** container maximum. Its normal side gutters are 48px, increase to 64px at 1600px and above, become 32px at 1000px and below, then 20px at 760px and below. Its collection uses an asymmetric 12-column composition, then two columns at 760px and one at 440px; the logical work order stays Vessel, Seat, Room. Viewer/specimen layouts stack at 760px. Major section separation is 144px normally and 88px in the narrower layout. Field-label gaps are 6px, and specimen component spacing has its own bounded values. Only `.specimen-panel` responds to the density choice; preference panels and image layouts do not.

## Image and art-direction policy

| Situation | Proposed treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Full object, artwork, document, or accurate comparison | Preserve the complete source with `contain` or its natural ratio; use a deliberate neutral surrounding field if needed. |
| Contextual or atmospheric composition | `cover` is permitted only with an intentional crop and focal-point record. Essential object detail still needs an uncropped view. |
| A tighter mobile crop is required | Prepare an appropriate source and express art direction with native responsive markup; do not download multiple CSS-hidden hero images. |
| Repeated collection cards | A consistent reserved frame can connect mixed ratios. Never stretch content to fill it. |
| Loading or unavailable image | Keep reserved space, associated title, caption, description, and credit; provide a truthful local recovery action when runtime recovery exists. |
| Different interface appearance | Preserve the image's own colors and semantic content. Adapt surrounding chrome rather than applying a dark-mode filter to the image. |

Represent content imagery with native `img`/`picture` rather than CSS backgrounds. Include meaningful intrinsic dimensions, useful context-dependent alternatives, and visible provenance near the media. The alternative describes the image's relevant information; a functional image's name describes its action. Do not put credit, surrounding prose, and every visible detail into an indiscriminate alt-text string.

Prioritize visible hero/LCP-candidate media and do not delay it behind lazy loading, entrance opacity, or JavaScript construction. Lower media may be lazy-loaded. A real project selects efficient formats and source sizes from actual assets and measures the resulting page. Native attributes and local successful loads alone do not prove bandwidth, LCP, CLS, or real-device performance.

The reference uses **three local AI-generated photography-style illustrations**: Vessel study at **1024 × 1536**, Seat study at **1254 × 1254**, and Room study at **1536 × 1024**. [Asset provenance](preview/assets/README.md) records the generation prompts, actual dimensions, and hashes. The retained unchanged PNGs total **7,002,794 bytes** and have no compressed/responsive derivative files. Reusing a source in hero, card, and viewer is one source in several contexts; a crop is not another photograph. The reference does not claim real products, real places, artists, prices, stock, or commercial photography. Its original raster fixtures are not a production responsive-image pipeline or network-performance claim.

The actual preview shows these sources without a contextual crop: collection images use their natural ratios, the hero's Room study uses its original 3:2 ratio, and detail images use `contain` with a **760px** height cap above the stacked layout. At 760px viewport width and below, the detail cap is removed. An inset 1px image outline at 10% black in light appearance or 10% white in dark appearance is decorative, not a necessary control boundary, and is outside the opaque-token calculations. Hero media loads eagerly with high fetch priority; collection/detail images are marked lazy. Only detail-article images expose explicit load/error/retry state; card and hero images retain native image/alt behavior.

## Components and bounded viewer behavior

| Component | Proposed rule |
| --- | --- |
| Primary action | Use action/on-action and the hover pair, a stable label, and a clear focus indicator. |
| Secondary action / prose link | Use ink, a necessary boundary where needed, and persistent underline for links in prose. |
| Input / select | Visible associated label, 16px entered text, sufficient boundary, and useful current value. |
| Collection card | Real media with title, context, and a native Inspect anchor; no hover-only detail or nested interactive card surface. |
| Current work selector | Three ordinary buttons with stable contextual names and `aria-pressed`; use an ink marker/boundary beyond surface color. |
| Detail article | Heading, image, text alternative, caption, provenance, image state, and a native return link. This is an inline region, not a modal. |
| Image recovery | A visible error description and explicit Retry for that image; completion cannot overwrite unrelated work metadata. |
| Collection feedback | Explicit count, understandable empty result, Clear filters, and concise polite feedback. |

The preview has three fixed work identities in the order **vessel, seat, room**. Search matches title/description case-insensitively; category is All, Objects, or Spaces. Filtering preserves the open detail and preference state. **Clear filters appears only in the empty-result region**. It resets both filters, preserves the selected work, and returns focus to Search rather than leaving it on a disappearing action.

Inspect is a real anchor, preserving normal modified and middle-click navigation. An unmodified scripted activation selects its inline article and focuses that article's heading. Ordinary view buttons remain available independently of collection filters, retain their own focus on activation, and announce the selected work. They are not a custom tab widget and need no invented arrow-key convention.

On initialization, a valid `#work-vessel`, `#work-seat`, or `#work-room` fragment selects and focuses that article; a valid live hash change does the same. A normal visit without a valid work fragment defaults to Vessel. This preserves meaningful native fragment destinations without storing the viewer state or inventing a history-based product router.

Back returns to the same Inspect anchor when that card remains visible. If filtering hides the source card, retain the filter and current detail, focus Search, and explain where the card went. Do not silently erase the user's filtering choices to simulate a successful return.

Each article keeps its own image/load/error/retry state. A completion for a noncurrent image cannot replace current metadata or create a misleading current-work announcement. Retry requests the same original asset URL, hides/disables its pending Retry action, and focuses the corresponding work heading with scroll position preserved. An error makes the broken visual transparent immediately while its frame, text alternative, caption, credit, and readable error remain. Test injected failures separately from ordinary asset health. The shipped preview must not manufacture broken requests or fake loading timers as a visual effect.

The viewer is not a cart, inventory service, product configurator, checkout, contact form, download service, or agent operation. A production catalog needs its own data, permissions, uncertainty, recovery, persistence, and transaction model.

## Appearance and accessibility

Support **Light, Dark, and System**, with **System as the preview default** and live device changes respected. Valid saved preferences are applied before the stylesheet where possible; malformed or unavailable storage retains usable defaults. Only appearance, specimen density, and motion preference persist under `interface-atlas-gallery-preview`. Search, category, selected work, and recovery state are not stored. Reload initializes fresh while honoring a valid work fragment as described above.

**Proposed focus:** 3px ink outline, 5px offset; forced-colors uses `Highlight`. Prevent clipping against every frame, selected item, and scroller. **Proposed comfortable target: 44px**; this is a usability choice rather than a claim about WCAG's minimum target size.

Use native landmarks, headings, links, controls, a skip link, and logical focus order. Images need useful alternatives and reserved space; meaning and recovery cannot depend on imagery alone. Without JavaScript, all three static detail articles, images, captions, metadata, anchors, and native specimen controls remain usable; runtime preferences, filtering, view selection, and retry remain unavailable with an explanation.

All content and viewer tasks update independently of animation. [Motion.md](motion.md) defines the optional feedback and immediate reduced/off alternative. Representative browser checks remain separate from complete accessibility, screen-reader testing, and user research.

# Gallery — optional effects

Revision: **0.1.0-draft**. Reviewed: **2026-10-15**.

Gallery is complete with static imagery, opaque surfaces, and immediate interaction. Image scale, whitespace, and restrained typography carry its identity. Every treatment below is an Atlas proposal; no Shopify effect, shader, carousel, or third-party implementation is imported.

## Framing and composition

- Keep media corners at the proposed **0px**, with a flat presentation rather than a decorative card shell.
- Use different visual weights for a deliberate hero/detail pairing while retaining useful DOM order.
- Reserve a source-aware frame before an image loads; background fill can make a contained object readable without pretending the fill belongs to the image.
- Place captions, names, provenance, states, and actions outside the media on opaque interface surfaces.
- Use the necessary control border or ink marker for interaction. A decorative line or photographic edge is not the sole selected-state signal.

These are composition options, not instructions to distort an asset. Full-object inspection remains complete; contextual crops require a focal-point decision and an available uncropped view when accuracy matters. A new crop does not acquire a new photographer or source identity.

## Restraint around images

The reference excludes hover zoom, image rollover, parallax, animated masks, autoplay slides, drifting collage elements, continuous texture, and cursor followers. Those effects add no necessary meaning to the bounded collection/viewer flow.

Do not invert or desaturate imagery to force a light/dark match. Preserve source colors in both appearances. Do not place essential interface text on a photograph and assume a gradient guarantees contrast; actual image luminance and crop vary. A production project choosing an overlay must test its final image/crop/text pairing and keep an independent readable route to the information.

## Generated fixture boundary

The preview's Vessel, Seat, and Room studies are **AI-generated photography-style illustrations**, created for Interface Atlas. They are not documentary photographs, actual products, named artists' work, or evidence of a photographer's commission. Read the [asset provenance record](preview/assets/README.md) for the retained prompts, dimensions, and hashes.

Imagery is core content in this reference rather than decorative filler, so useful alternatives, captions, and text descriptions remain available. Loading and error state preserve those descriptions. A visual asset failure cannot make the collection unnamed or eliminate its recovery route.

## Motion and implementation

Only optional **180ms color/background/border feedback** accompanies controls when motion is allowed. There are no transform/opacity entrance effects or image animations. State and focus change immediately; follow [motion.md](motion.md).

No image library, renderer, remote font service, or effect runtime is required.
