# Gallery — motion specification

Revision: **0.1.0-draft**. Reviewed: **2026-10-15**.

Gallery's identity comes from still imagery and composition. **All timings and behavior in this document are Atlas proposals**, not extracted Dawn/Horizon animation values. No animation library or upstream effect implementation is included.

## Optional control feedback

| Property | Proposed behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Color, background color, border color | **180ms**, `cubic-bezier(.2, 0, 0, 1)`, only when motion is enabled and the OS permits it. |
| Focus outline | Immediate. |
| Filtering, selected work, image state, and recovery | Immediate; no waiting for transitions. |
| Layout, dimensions, scrolling, image transforms, opacity, and entrance | No animation in the reference. |

Use an explicit property list rather than `transition: all`. Feedback can help show a native control's state, but the final state must already be represented by semantics and readable content. Do not communicate selected work, loading, availability, error, or completion by motion alone.

## Preference and static behavior

- **Motion off** removes optional transitions.
- **OS reduced motion** overrides the preview's enabled choice and makes feedback immediate.
- Changing the OS preference live updates the behavior; the user's stored enabled choice does not override the OS restriction.
- No images move, autoplay, cycle, fade in, zoom on hover, or wait for animation completion.
- No timer, visibility listener, or animation-API lifecycle is needed for continuous motion because the reference has none.

The finite change of an opaque control color does not start an ongoing process. There is no automatic motion to restart when a document becomes visible again. Do not add an entrance effect that hides the initial hero or delays discovery of its image.

## Image state and focus

Detail-image loading and retry follow real image events, not decorative timers. A failed image retains its description, caption, and credit, with an explicit local Retry control when JavaScript is available. Its failed visual becomes transparent immediately rather than fading. Completion for another image cannot change the active work's metadata or misleadingly announce that the active work completed. Retry hides its own pending control and focuses the corresponding work heading without animated scrolling.

Inspect focuses the selected article heading. View buttons retain their focus. Back follows the collection's visibility-aware recovery rule, and Clear filters returns focus to Search. These actions do not depend on a transition ending; there is no animated scrolling.

## Project adaptation

If a project introduces a carousel, zoom, video, or other movement, document its user purpose, control, reduced-motion/static alternative, media accessibility, and measured performance separately. Gallery's static preview does not validate such an adaptation.

Read [preview notes](preview/README.md) for the implemented local scope and [validation.md](validation.md) for the actual browser evidence. No real-device performance or complete accessibility claim follows from the 180ms timing proposal.

# Layered

A spacious application direction built from purposeful opaque tonal planes, friendly geometric sans typography, repeated rounded geometry, and selective elevation. Navigation, working content, supporting context, and a temporary editor have different roles without turning every region into a shadowed card.

Layered is an **original Interface Atlas synthesis for Tamir (Phi Vuong Tuong Tam), prepared with Codex AI assistance**. Google's Material Design 3 supplies conceptual references for surface roles, elevation, shape coherence, adaptive composition, and states. Microsoft's Fluent 2 supplies a separate comparison for opaque material, depth, and readable hierarchy. No design-system implementation, token package, artwork, screenshots, prose, or font software is imported. Every numerical rule and the preview's composition and workflow are Atlas proposals.

This is a complete visual direction rather than a teal palette variant. Editorial emphasizes serif-led reading and publication rhythm; Precision emphasizes compact, flat operational work. Layered gives consumer tasks more room, uses tonal planes to establish context, and reserves raised treatment for a deliberate temporary editor. Neither glass nor continuous motion defines its identity.

## Suitability

These are Atlas design assessments, not measured usability or product outcomes.

| Project type | Fit | Reason and adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Consumer application | Strong | Comfortable controls and distinct working regions suit ordinary browsing, selection, and editing. Define the actual navigation model and persistence. |
| Personal planner | Strong | Small projects and checklist tasks can remain readable without a dense analytics shell. Real dates, reminders, sync, and recovery need a project contract. |
| Learning workspace | Strong | Spacious task groupings can separate current work, supporting material, and settings. Enrollment, durable progress, assessment, and access remain product decisions. |
| Team project space | Conditional | Tonal composition supports projects and contextual editing. Membership, collaboration conflicts, authority, and audit behavior are not supplied here. |
| Settings interface | Strong | Grouped controls and a restrained modal editor support focused changes. Explain immediate versus saved effects and reversible versus consequential actions. |
| Portfolio or publication | Conditional | Use an application-like index when it helps navigation. Layered's comfortable workspace composition is not a substitute for an image or long-reading system. |
| Dense agent operations | Conditional | Add explicit execution, attention, connection, approval, and pending-command dimensions. A rounded card does not establish an agent's authority or confirmed outcome. |
| Image-led catalog or expressive campaign | Strained | Application surfaces can compete with the primary imagery or poster composition. Gallery or Pulse may provide a more direct starting point. |

Record the selected fit and adaptations in the consuming project's design document. Load [shared Agent Experience guidance](../../knowledge/agent-experience.md) only when relevant to that project's tasks.

# Layered — design specification

Revision: **0.1.0-draft**. Reviewed: **2026-10-15**.

Layered is an original Atlas synthesis informed by Material Design 3 and a separate Fluent 2 comparison. **All numerical values, role mappings, typography selections, geometry, timings, layouts, and workflow rules below are Atlas proposals.** Reference observations identify concepts rather than imported tokens or implementation. Read [sources and credits](sources.md) for the exact scope.

## Color tokens and surface roles

| Role | Light | Dark | Proposed purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Page | `#EAF2F1` | `#101C1C` | Application base. |
| Low | `#DFEBE9` | `#172626` | Navigation plane and quiet structural context. |
| Surface | `#F7FBFA` | `#1E3030` | Main content and project regions. |
| Raised | `#FFFFFF` | `#273C3B` | Inputs and temporary modal editor. |
| Tint | `#D5EAE5` | `#294C46` | Selected context and deliberate emphasis. |
| Secondary | `#F2E6DA` | `#43372E` | Quiet supporting panel. |
| Ink | `#172F2C` | `#E7F3EF` | Primary text, selected text, and explicit markers. |
| Muted | `#405E58` | `#B4CEC5` | Readable supporting text. |
| Primary | `#185C50` | `#A2D6C5` | Action fill or underlined action text on a named neutral surface. |
| On primary | `#FFFFFF` | `#12382E` | Text/icons on the primary action fill only. |
| Border | `#58766E` | `#8AABA1` | Necessary input/control boundaries. |
| Focus | `#6D3B83` | `#E7B6F4` | Immediate external focus indicator. |
| Error | `#972F3A` | `#FFB3BE` | Error text and meaningful invalid boundary. |

**Reference observation:** Material's surface/container distinction supports regional hierarchy; Fluent's solid material shows that depth does not require translucency. Layered uses its own six opaque background roles rather than importing a Material palette, dynamic-color algorithm, Fluent ramp, or platform material.

Map roles by purpose. Navigation stays Low when repositioned; working content stays Surface; editing fields stay Raised. Dark planes become lighter as they rise. Light planes need not follow a mechanical luminance staircase: regional purpose, coherent contrast, and readable content matter more than a literal inversion.

Use Ink on Tint for selected labels and markers. Primary can be used as text on the six named backgrounds, but On primary is a separate action pair. Do not use On primary as ordinary text. Hover keeps the action's foreground/fill pairing and adds explicit boundary feedback; no unverified lighter action color is introduced.

Supporting labels are not faded with opacity. Priority is readable **Normal**, **Focus**, or **Later**, not an invented success/warning/danger signal. Error includes a message and an associated field or summary; a red outline alone is insufficient. A decorative divider may use a low-opacity Border, but that composed line cannot identify an input or carry a numerical necessary-boundary claim.

## Typography and hierarchy

Proposed named family: **Plus Jakarta Sans**, normal **400/500/600/700**, with `"Segoe UI", Arial, sans-serif` fallbacks. Use a single coherent family for application headings and body. A technical specimen may use local `Consolas, "Courier New", monospace`; it is not another selected brand family. No fonts are bundled or fetched.

| Role | Proposed size | Weight | Line height | Tracking |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intro/display | `clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 4rem)` | 600 | 1.1 | `-0.035em` |
| Section heading | `1.75rem` | 600 | 1.25 | Normal |
| Card/detail heading | `1.25rem` | 600 | 1.35 | Normal |
| Body and extended reading | `1rem` | 400 | 1.6 | Normal |
| Labels and supporting metadata | `0.875rem` | 500 | 1.5 | Normal |
| Input and control text | At least `1rem` | 400/500/600 | At least 1.5 | Normal |
| Technical specimen | `0.875rem` | 400 | 1.5 | Normal |

Use sentence case, a single primary heading, and continuous semantic heading levels. Align headings, task labels, form labels and actions to predictable starting edges. Keep extended passages around **65ch**; do not stretch reading text merely because a pane has room. Use tabular numerals only for useful comparisons such as task counts.

Preserve full project names, validation messages, and task text. Wrap long titles, identifiers, and Vietnamese text. Do not hide essential names behind hover-only tooltips or fixed-height clipping. An actual project selects the exact font package, retained OFL notice, supported weights/scripts, and fallback behavior. A CSS family name does not establish that Plus Jakarta Sans rendered.

## Spacing, density, and responsive layout

Proposed scale: **4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96px**. Use 8px between a label and field, 12–16px between related controls, and 24–32px between working groups. Generous spacing expresses task relationships; it does not justify rows of empty decorative containers.

- Comfortable is the default. Proposed panel inset: **24px**.
- Compact adapts **only the neutral specimen inset to 16px** in the reference. It does not shrink workspace cards, text, navigation, dialog fields, or targets.
- Control and navigation hit areas remain at least **44px × 44px**. Checkbox labels provide the usable area around the native input.
- Proposed main maximum: **1440px**, with **24px** side gutters and **16px** narrow gutters.
- A **224px** navigation plane is suitable where content retains room; stack it into a useful compact navigation region at **960px** and below in the reference.
- Project cards can use three, two, or one columns according to content fit. Record the actual preview breakpoints in [preview notes](preview/README.md); a column count is not a universal project rule.

**Reference observation:** Material's adaptive guidance preserves functional meaning while resizing, reflowing, revealing panes, or exchanging equivalent navigation. Layered's native anchors and content order remain useful at every width; it does not ship an official Material navigation component.

Keep the same logical DOM order as the visual reading order. Present project discovery before detail; selected detail can remain available even when a filter hides its card. Avoid sticky regions or fixed bottom bars that cover focus, form errors, text, or browser zoom. A supporting pane should earn its space through a useful task; do not create a third column simply to fill the viewport.

## Shape, material, and depth

| Element | Proposed geometry or treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Panels and project cards | **24px** radius; opaque role fill; no resting shadow needed. |
| Inputs and ordinary controls | **12px** radius with a necessary boundary. |
| Navigation/current-location indicator | **999px** pill where it fits the content; explicit current text or semantic state. |
| Modal editor | **28px** radius; opaque Raised surface in the native top layer. |
| Modal shadow | Optional `0 24px 64px rgba(0,0,0,.24)`; original Atlas proposal. |

Repeated shape roles create coherence. Nested containers should fit within their parent's inset without awkward corner collisions. A pill is appropriate for a short navigation label, not automatically for a paragraph or input. Do not apply drop shadows to every card or inset bevels to simulate physical controls.

The modal's optional translucent backdrop separates a blocking task from the surrounding workspace; its content and controls remain opaque. Backdrop compositing and shadow are not covered by opaque token calculations. [Effects.md](effects.md) explains the boundary; no backdrop blur, acrylic, Mica, glass, image texture, or required shader is part of the theme.

## Components and state

| Component | Proposed behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Primary action | Primary/On primary pair, useful verb, stable dimensions, necessary boundary feedback and visible focus. |
| Secondary action | Ink on an opaque named surface; meaningful boundary; clear relation to the main action. |
| Navigation | Real destinations, readable labels and current location. Use native anchors; do not invent tab or menu semantics. |
| Project card | A real contextual **Open TITLE** anchor, title, category, priority text and computed sample-task count. Current context also has a readable marker. |
| Search/category | Visible labels, native controls, useful result count, clear empty recovery and no loss of selected detail. |
| Checklist | Native associated checkbox labels; text and checked state remain meaningful independently of color. |
| Input/select | Visible associated label, helpful constraints, Raised background, Border, native semantics and local error association. |
| Modal editor | Accessible name, intentional first focus, native modality, reachable Save/Cancel, Escape discard, useful focus return. |
| Error summary | Linked list naming invalid fields, focused summary heading after failed Save, inline field feedback. No duplicate assertive alert is required. |
| Revert | Explicitly restores only the named project's initial title, priority and tasks; disabled when unchanged with readable explanatory context. |
| Task counts | Derived from actual fixture checkboxes; identify sample tasks rather than presenting invented analytics or achievement claims. |

Represent default, hover, focus, pressed, current/selected, disabled and invalid states separately where appropriate. A selected item can still have focus. Focus is immediate and visible; a tonal wash alone is not the entire indicator. Disabled runtime controls retain a visible explanation rather than looking like a loading product.

## Bounded editing and recovery contract

The original reference uses three fictional projects and nine sample tasks. It is an illustrative consumer workspace, not an account, backend, agent system, or synchronization demo.

1. Search compares saved title and description case-insensitively; category narrows the same fixed-order list. Filtering preserves current detail, task state, saved edits and preferences. Empty-result Clear resets both filters and focuses Search.
2. An unmodified primary Open activation selects its static article and focuses that article's heading. Other anchor behavior remains native. A valid initial or live `#project-ID` fragment selects and focuses its matching article. These are ordinary links, not custom tabs.
3. Task activation changes that project's saved local checkbox state and recomputes its count and the aggregate. It does not change unrelated titles, filters or another project's tasks.
4. Edit copies saved title/priority into a separate draft. The native named dialog opens with the title input focused; surrounding content is inert through native modal behavior. Filtering out a card does not remove the selected article's Edit action.
5. Save trims title, requires **1–60 characters**, and accepts only **normal**, **focus**, or **later**. Invalid input mutates no saved state, stays open, adds associated inline errors and linked summary, and focuses the summary heading.
6. Valid Save updates title and priority together, refreshes reflected names, filter results and changed-state controls, then closes and returns focus to the opener. Tasks remain unchanged. Render user text as text; do not interpret it as markup. There is no asynchronous spinner or fake network acknowledgement.
7. Cancel and native Escape discard the draft, preserve saved state, and return focus to Edit. Outside clicks do not dismiss. Reopening reads the saved values rather than an abandoned draft.
8. Revert restores only the current project's initial title, priority and tasks. Preserve other projects, filters, selected detail and preferences. Focus the detail heading because Revert becomes disabled after restoration.
9. If the native modal API is missing or opening fails, explain that editing is unavailable and disable Edit actions; task, filtering and native navigation remain useful. Do not replace a failed modal with an inaccessible imitation.
10. Save only appearance, specimen density and motion preference. All workspace changes reset on reload, apart from a valid location fragment selecting its corresponding static article. State this boundary plainly.

Real projects must separately specify durable save semantics, connection state, data ownership, authorization, concurrent changes, retry, recovery and undo scope. If agents can act, define scope, approvals, pending versus confirmed effects and audit history using [Agent Experience guidance](../../knowledge/agent-experience.md). This local editor grants no agent authority.

## Appearance and accessibility

Support **Light, Dark and System**, with System the reference default. Restore a validated saved choice before the stylesheet where practical, follow live system appearance when System is selected, and keep usable defaults when storage is malformed, unavailable or blocked.

Proposed focus: **3px solid Focus with 3px offset**, outside the target on a named neutral surface. Check actual adjacency, clipping and modal placement; use system **Highlight** in forced colors. A 44px comfort target is an Atlas choice, not a claim about WCAG's minimum.

Use semantic landmarks, useful section navigation, skip link, native labeled fields and logical keyboard order. No JavaScript leaves every project article readable through native anchors; runtime controls and task mutations remain disabled with a visible explanation, while ordinary specimen fields can work. A closed dialog remains hidden even if browser default styling is absent.

Optional feedback becomes immediate under motion-off or OS reduced motion. Content, task state, validation, focus and modal closure never wait for animation. Each consuming project checks actual fonts, translated text, narrow reflow, text resizing, browser zoom, keyboard access, assistive technology, forced colors and rendered contrast. A native element and arithmetic do not certify the whole interface.

## Numerical contrast record

Calculated **2026-10-15** using opaque sRGB relative luminance; no alpha compositing, shadow or backdrop is included. The six backgrounds are **Page, Low, Surface, Raised, Tint and Secondary**.

| Pair | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ink on Page | 12.48:1 | 15.32:1 |
| Ink, minimum across all six | 11.31:1 | 8.33:1 |
| Muted, minimum across all six | 5.65:1 | 5.67:1 |
| Primary as text, minimum across all six | 6.23:1 | 5.85:1 |
| Border, minimum across all six | 3.95:1 | 3.80:1 |
| Focus, minimum across all six | 6.43:1 | 5.59:1 |
| Error, minimum across all six | 6.01:1 | 5.61:1 |
| On primary on Primary action fill | 7.82:1 | 7.95:1 |

For every six-surface minimum above, **Tint is the limiting background in both appearances**. Selected Ink-on-Tint is therefore 11.31:1 light and 8.33:1 dark. Proposed action hover retains the same verified colors.

The six planes are grouping fills rather than necessary control outlines. Do not infer that their mutual contrast reaches 3:1. # Layered — optional effects

Revision: **0.1.0-draft**. Reviewed: **2026-10-15**.

Layered is complete with opaque tonal surfaces, coherent geometry, readable content and immediate state changes. Every effect and numerical treatment below is an **Atlas proposal**. No Material or Fluent effect implementation, shape library, icon set, shader, renderer or third-party artwork is imported.

## Tonal composition

Assign a surface a useful role before adding another container. A Low navigation plane, Surface working region, Secondary supporting panel and Raised editor can establish context without multiple shadow ramps. Selection uses Tint, readable Ink and an explicit current marker; it remains recognizable without interpreting the hue.

Keep working surfaces opaque in both appearances. Quiet static geometric artwork may echo the same rounded vocabulary in a header or empty state, but it must remain decorative and must not carry a project's name, task status, count or action. Code-native shapes are original Atlas artwork rather than copied Material shapes or logos. Artwork cannot hide useful content during initialization.

Repeated **24px panels**, **12px controls**, **999px navigation pills** and a **28px modal** form the proposed geometry. Do not add an unrelated radius to every card. Avoid nested card shells when a heading and space already communicate grouping. Preserve meaningful reading order when arranging a decorative composition beside content.

## Selective elevation

An optional original modal shadow is `0 24px 64px rgba(0,0,0,.24)`. It suggests the temporary editor sits above the workspace. The native modal's opaque Raised fill, visible boundaries, accessible name and focus behavior still work without that shadow. Ordinary project cards do not need a resting shadow.

A translucent backdrop can dim the blocked workspace while the editor is open. This is separation for a modal task, not a translucent content material. Backdrop and shadow are composed visuals outside the opaque color arithmetic; inspect actual light/dark combinations and forced-colors fallback. Never put essential text on the dimmed background and treat its contrast as an active dialog control.

There is no required glass, backdrop blur, Mica, acrylic, neumorphic inset shading, glow, grain, photographic texture, parallax, cursor follower or persistent effect. The fictional workspace neither samples a desktop wallpaper nor reproduces a native operating-system material.

## States and motion

Use a clear boundary for controls and a visible focus outline independent of optional background feedback. A tonal selection and a focus indicator can appear together. Priority labels remain text; decorative artwork and colors do not establish permissions, safety, completion or authority.

Only optional **160ms color/background/border feedback** accompanies ordinary control interaction when motion is allowed. Focus, selection, filtering, checklist counts, form validation and modal closure are immediate. No ripple, scale, entrance, fade or moving illustration is part of the reference. Follow [motion.md](motion.md).

Material Design and Fluent are credited conceptual comparisons in [sources.md](sources.md). Their software licenses do not clear copied website assets or brand identity. # Layered — motion specification

Revision: **0.1.0-draft**. Reviewed: **2026-10-15**.

Layered uses quiet optional feedback while application state stays immediate. **Every timing, easing and behavioral rule here is an Atlas proposal**, not a Material motion token, Fluent animation sample or native-platform implementation. No animation library or external effect code is included.

## Optional feedback

| Property or event | Proposed treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Control color, background color and border color | **160ms**, `cubic-bezier(.2, 0, 0, 1)`, only with motion enabled and no OS reduced-motion request. |
| Focus outline | Immediate. |
| Current project, filters, task checks and computed counts | Immediate; selection semantics and text do not wait for a visual transition. |
| Modal opening, closing, validation and focus return | Immediate; no opacity, translation, scale or delayed interaction. |
| Layout, dimensions, scrolling, artwork and initial content | Static, with no animation. |

Use an explicit CSS property list, not `transition: all`. Do not animate errors into view, delay focus until a transition ends, or interpolate a task count as if it were an analytics achievement. State changes are represented by native controls, names, messages and current context regardless of feedback.

## Preferences and static behavior

- Motion-off removes the optional transition.
- OS reduced motion overrides the stored enabled choice.
- Live changes to the OS preference update eligibility without changing saved application data.
- All content starts visible. No reveal, entrance, opacity gate, ripple, hover scale, auto-scrolling or continuous loop is required.
- No animation API, frame renderer, animation-completion promise or document-visibility lifecycle is needed for this reference's finite CSS color feedback.

The user can still search, open a project, check tasks, edit, recover from an invalid field, cancel or revert with motion off. A dialog is never held open for a closing animation; native inertness and focus return follow actual dialog state.

## Focus and recovery

Opening a project focuses its heading. Editing focuses the title field. Failed Save focuses the linked error summary heading; the user's draft remains available. Save, Cancel and native Escape close the editor and restore the opener. Revert focuses the current detail heading because its initiating control becomes disabled. Empty-result Clear focuses Search because the empty-result action disappears.

These behaviors use immediate focus rather than animated scrolling. They are local workflow decisions, not proof that every assistive technology behaves identically. Read [preview notes](preview/README.md) for the implemented scope and [validation.md](validation.md) for observed browser evidence.

If a consuming project adds pane transitions, an animated overlay, notifications, video or another moving element, document its purpose, control, interruption behavior, reduced/static alternative, and measured cost separately. Layered's static reference does not validate that new motion or establish real-device performance.

# Play

Warm cream and deep violet surfaces, colorful supporting panels, bold sans-serif headings, rounded geometry, and hard offset shadows give work a tactile character. Play supports expressive presentation while keeping controls, reading, and task states clear. Brief feedback is sufficient; animated decoration is optional.

This entry adapts the Play direction in **Tamir (Phi Vuong Tuong Tam)'s portfolio**, retaining observed design values and identifying portable Atlas proposals. Manrope is the principal typeface, with JetBrains Mono for short technical labels. Atlas's original preview applies the direction to a fictional creative portfolio and a local brief builder.

| Dense operations or analytics | Conditional | Requires additional density, chart, data, and update rules. Reduce large display type and decorative shadow frequency around repeated work. |

## Typography and hierarchy

**Source observation:** Play uses the configured Manrope sans family for both ordinary and formerly editorial text; the Play selector removes the italic serif treatment. Its hero is 800 weight with `-0.065em` tracking, an underlined accent line, and a large shared responsive scale. Project headings use 700 weight and `-0.06em` tracking. JetBrains Mono is configured at 400/500 weights for short technical roles.

**Atlas proposal:** use Manrope for readable interface text, with a small JetBrains Mono role for indexes or identifiers. Moderate display tracking and a portable scale keep the source hero's treatment from spreading to controls and body text.

| Role | Proposed family / weight | Size | Line height | Tracking |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Portfolio display | Manrope 800 | `clamp(3.5rem, 8.1vw, 8.75rem)` | `0.95` | `-0.035em` |
| Major section heading | Manrope 700/800 | `clamp(2rem, 4.2vw, 3.75rem)` | `1.04` | `-0.025em` |
| Card / detail heading | Manrope 700/800 | `1.75rem` | `1.15` | `-0.02em` |
| Body / extended reading | Manrope 400 | `1rem` | `1.6` | Normal |
| Label / short supporting text | Manrope 400/600 | `0.875rem` | `1.5` | Normal |
| Text input | Manrope 400 | `1rem` | `1.5` | Normal |
| Short index / technical value | JetBrains Mono 400/500 | `0.875rem` | `1.5` | Normal |

The portfolio display is a deliberate expressive choice. Use a smaller project-specific heading scale in working forms and learning tasks; controls do not need the portfolio display size. Keep a single main heading and continuous semantic levels. Sentence case suits actions and reading. A short uppercase index may be decorative supporting text.

Prose measure: about **65 characters**. Avoid tight tracking in paragraphs, errors, labels, or identifiers. Allow long names and translated labels to wrap. Use tabular numerals for comparable data. A preview-specific 12px monospace eyebrow or sticker label is limited to short decorative supporting text; meaningful form labels remain 14px, and body/input text remains 16px.

The preview names the families but contains no font files or remote font loading. Intended Manrope/JetBrains Mono rendering requires a separate check of installed or vendored versions, weights, scripts, wrapping, and fallback. Manrope's source setup requests Latin and Vietnamese; the source mono setup requests Latin. Those choices are observations, not a promise of every project's language coverage.

## Spacing, density, and layout

All rules in this section are **Atlas proposals**.

- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, and 64px.
- Comfortable is the default: 24px panel padding. Compact adaptation uses 16px in selected component specimens.
- Keep labels 8px from their controls, related controls 12–16px apart, and independent regions 24–32px apart.
- Body text remains 16px, form labels 14px, text inputs 16px, and action areas at least 44px in both densities.
- Begin with 16px outer gutters; increase to 24px when content permits. A typical proposed content maximum is 1280px.
- Share starting edges for headings, project text, form labels, and actions. Add columns when both content regions retain readable widths.

A portfolio can use a large introduction followed by a small project grid and readable case-study disclosures. A creative task can put input beside a persistent review region when space permits. Their ordering follows the task; the theme does not prescribe one universal page grid.

The reference preview keeps portfolio cards and the brief builder at 24px base padding, with a responsive 20px adaptation at widths up to 384px. Its density selector changes component-card and table-cell padding only, from 24px to 16px. Its composition selects a 1296px content maximum and 40px desktop outer gutters, falling to 20px at widths up to 672px and 16px at widths up to 384px. These are original preview choices, independent of specimen density. Compact mode does not shrink control areas or establish an operations-dashboard density.

On narrow screens, use one column in meaningful DOM order. Keep errors, review details, and the primary action close to their context. Wrap long input-derived values and preserve text at 200% resizing and zoom. A necessary wide table may use a labeled keyboard-focusable scrolling region; ordinary content must not force page-wide horizontal scrolling.

## Geometry and elevation

**Source observation:** panel radius is **30px** and control radius **14px**. The theme shadow token is `4px 5px 0 #2b203d` in light appearance and `4px 5px 0 #0c0612` in dark. Source Play primary buttons use an additional 3px/3px ink shadow. Project cards and lab cards use ink boundaries; a source profile backing tilts 2 degrees.

**Atlas proposal:** retain 30px/14px radii and hard offset panel shadows for selected expressive surfaces. Use a firm ink boundary to connect the fill and shadow. Keep form labels, inputs, body text, and action rows level. Avoid placing a shadow on every nested region; one primary surface can carry the tactile treatment.

Static stickers, simple original shapes, and a small decorative tilt may support a portfolio. Contain them outside essential copy and input areas, mark purely decorative content appropriately, and preserve visible focus. [Effects.md](effects.md) defines optional scope and acceptance checks.

## Components and task states

The following contracts are **Atlas proposals**.

| Component | Proposed behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Primary action | Verified action/on-action pair, meaningful verb, 14px radius, at least 44px area, stable layout, and visible focus. |
| Secondary action | Readable ink on a neutral or verified tinted surface, with a visible necessary boundary. |
| Project card | Useful heading and description; an explicit case-study destination or native disclosure. Keep independent links independently operable. |
| Input | Visible associated label, 16px input text, proposed control border, help connected to the field, and nearby corrective error text. |
| Option group | Visible group label, native controls, and text identifying the selected value. Color is supplementary. |
| Disclosure | Prefer native details/summary for optional case evidence. Its open state and contents must remain usable without animation. |
| Review | Show a stable snapshot of the submitted input, the scope, and what confirmation would request. Provide an explicit edit action. |
| Pending request | Persistent textual state and relevant context. Avoid repeated confirmation and do not represent a request as successful execution. |
| Status | Meaningful text and optional marker on checked surfaces; explain whether it describes a local preview, request, acknowledgement, or real outcome. |

Define default, hover, focus, pressed/selected, unavailable, pending, failure, and completed states as appropriate. Do not make supporting text unreadable when its associated control is disabled. Errors explain what to correct and preserve entered data.

**Proposed brief workflow:** editing → validation → review → request pending → acknowledgement. Client-side checks are feedback, not server-side trust. Put understandable errors near the relevant inputs and provide deliberate focus to the error or review context, informed by [W3C WAI form guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/). Keep the reviewed snapshot stable; returning to edit should preserve draft input.

The reference preview manually advances a fictional request after review. It sends no network request, starts no agent, and does not persist brief contents across reloads. A request and its manual demonstration acknowledgement have distinct text. Editing after the local receipt preserves draft input and clears the current receipt/snapshot before a new review; this demonstrates no remote versioning or undo. Real projects must define authority, server validation, duplicate protection, recovery, audit records, and backend acknowledgement in their own contract, using relevant [Agent Experience guidance](../../knowledge/agent-experience.md).

## Appearance and accessibility

**Source observation:** the global focus outline is **3px ink with 5px offset**, changing to system `Highlight` under forced colors. The portfolio has additional local focus styles; this package retains the global dimensions as its reference-preview focus treatment.

**Atlas proposals:** support light, dark, and system appearance; apply saved preferences before paint where possible and follow live system changes when system is selected. Invalid or unavailable storage retains usable defaults. Honor OS reduced motion from first paint and keep content/state changes immediate under reduced motion or motion-off.

Use native landmarks, a useful skip link, associated labels, logical focus order, readable state text, and underlined prose links. Preserve keyboard access and text selection. A 44px area is a comfort target selected by Atlas, not a claim about the WCAG minimum. Check actual focus adjacency and clipping, forced colors, narrow reflow, 200% text resizing, zoom, and screen-reader information in the project.

# Play — optional effects

Play's rounded surfaces, bold typography, colorful regions, firm boundaries, and offset shadows establish its character. Optional effects should support the content. [Design rules](design.md) define the readable layer and [motion rules](motion.md) define immediate fallbacks.

## Tactile surfaces and static stickers

**Source observation:** the Play shadow token offsets a hard shadow 4px right and 5px down, using dark ink in light appearance and `#0c0612` in dark. Source project/lab cards have ink boundaries, primary buttons have 3px/3px ink shadows, the emblem is a small yellow marked shape, and the profile backing has a 2-degree tilt.

**Atlas proposal:** use the retained hard panel shadow selectively around expressive project surfaces and component specimens. Keep inputs, reading, labels, and action rows level. Static original CSS shapes or a small sticker may sit beside an introduction when they leave meaningful copy, hit targets, and focus clear. The reference preview's composition and shapes are original Atlas work.

[Samuel Breznjak's Neobrutalism components](https://www.neobrutalism.dev/docs) is an **additional Atlas comparison** for prominent boundaries and offset shadows. It does not establish that Tamir used those components. Its September 2026 documentation describes Base UI components and light-only palettes; Play's dark values come from Tamir's source. No Neobrutalism component, palette, icon, or implementation is imported.

No animation runtime is required for these static treatments. Use a system-color boundary in forced colors when shadows and fills are unavailable. A shadow cannot be the only indicator of selection, focus, or state.

## Optional sphere artwork

**Portfolio inspiration credit:** [Interactive Hero Backgrounds](https://21st.dev/@ravikatiyar162/components/interactive-hero-backgrounds), published by **Ravi Katiyar / @ravikatiyar162**.

**Observed local adaptation:** Tamir's pinned hero-artwork notes describe original Canvas 2D scenes inspired by selected 21st.dev interaction concepts. Play has seven shaded spheres that float, repel the pointer, collide, and scatter on activation before returning toward their home positions. This is an original local adaptation, not imported catalog implementation.

The source renderer mounts for a fine pointer and hover-capable desktop at least 1024px wide within its visible theme scope. Its native effect button has an accessible label and keyboard activation. Reduced motion or motion-off produces static artwork and disables effect activation. Offscreen and hidden-tab observation stops animation frames; pixel density is capped at 2, and listeners/observers are cleaned up when replaced or removed.

**Atlas proposal:** a project may select original sphere decoration only after checking text/background composition, performance, keyboard behavior, focus visibility, reduced/static fallback, and lifecycle cleanup. Omit it on small or coarse-pointer screens and keep content useful when canvas or script is unavailable. Do not place required status or instructions inside the canvas.

The reference preview selects no canvas, sphere loop, or sphere activation. The external component's reuse terms remain **unresolved**; its reference URL is not permission to copy code, assets, or dependencies. An actual import needs its own verified version, license, notices, and focused validation.

## Optional star and color-trail cursor

**Source observation:** the Play cursor is a supplementary asterisk mark with three small colored trails. It preserves the native pointer and hit targets. The follower operates for mouse input on fine-pointer, hover-capable devices, hides over text inputs, textarea, select, editable content and frames, and hides on keyboard use, blur, pointer leave, hidden tabs, reduced motion, motion-off, or forced colors. Animation frames stop once the follower settles.

**Atlas proposal:** a cursor effect is an optional expressive portfolio selection. It must not replace the native pointer, intercept events, obscure text editing, imitate a loading state, or become necessary for locating a control. It requires its own eligibility, lifecycle, visibility, and performance checks. The preview includes no cursor follower or trail, and copies no source Lucide mark.

## Acceptance checks

Check actual composited text contrast, readable selection, visible focus, contained decoration, narrow reflow, 200% text resizing, keyboard use, native text selection, forced colors, and motion preferences. Decoration must not change reading order, obscure errors, or provide the only state meaning.

Keep static styling, continuously animated decoration, and request-state feedback separate. [Sources.md](sources.md) preserves the creator, inspiration, and reuse boundaries; any imported package or artwork requires a new source record.

# Play — motion specification

Play's tactile character can come from static geometry and shadows. Motion is an optional project choice; readable content and correct state must be immediate. The reference preview selects brief control feedback and no entrance sequence, sphere animation, cursor follower, animated scrolling, or continuous loop.

| `app/themes.css` shared controls | Press scale `0.96`; 2px/-2px arrow translation on hover | Interaction feedback, not essential meaning. The source removes transforms under reduced motion or motion-off. |

## Portable project rules

Every rule in this section is an **Atlas proposal** unless identified as retained.

| Role | Selected Atlas treatment | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Control color and border feedback | Retain 240ms duration and the source theme curve; apply it uniformly | Atlas normalization of the source shorthand. Keep layout and target dimensions stable. |
| Optional tactile press | Up to 2px diagonal translation | Original Atlas CSS choice, selected by the preview for enabled button presses with the static shadow retained. It is not a reproduction of the source spring runtime or 0.96 scale. |
| Initial content and preference, error, review, or request state changes | Immediate state/content updates | Do not hide useful content behind an entrance or use a timing as an artificial processing delay. |
| Native disclosure | Immediate content and state | The preview uses native details/summary without animated height or opacity. |
| Optional card tilt | Deliberate project selection only | Keep essential text level and the hit area usable. The source hover values are observations, not preview defaults. |
| Background updates | Preserve focus and reading position | Announce meaningful state changes without moving the active target. |

Keep a request's pending label visible until real acknowledgement in a real project. Decorative feedback cannot confirm a backend action. An optional completion flourish must follow confirmed completion and leave a persistent textual record.

An additional spring, overlay, entrance, or reward needs its own project selection, implementation terms, and focused checks. The package requires no animation library, and the preview does not import Framer Motion/Motion.

## Reduced motion and user control

These are **Atlas proposals**: honor `prefers-reduced-motion` from first paint, including live changes. OS reduced motion overrides a saved “Motion enabled” preference. A visible motion control may independently disable feedback.

Under reduced motion or motion-off, make transitions immediate, remove press/hover transforms and entrance offsets, keep navigation scrolling immediate, and render all useful content in its final visible state. Preserve validation, pending-request text, review context, acknowledgements, and status announcements.

A future sphere effect may use a static composition or omit decoration, while leaving the page readable. A future cursor follower must be absent when motion is reduced or disabled. Do not replace a stopped effect with hidden information.

Check initial visibility, live system preference changes, saved preferences, keyboard focus, press/hover behavior, and no-JavaScript content. The reference preview's browser evidence covers its implemented feedback only; it does not validate the source's spring runtime, sphere renderer, cursor follower, or any unselected entrance.

# Precision

Cool neutral layers, a deliberate blue action color, restrained typography, aligned data, and compact geometry support repeated operational work. Lists and details share context; status copy separates what was requested from what is confirmed. Brief feedback keeps controls responsive and positions stable.

Precision is an **original Interface Atlas synthesis**, developed for **Tamir (Phi Vuong Tuong Tam) with Codex AI assistance**. It studies concepts from **IBM's Carbon Design System** and **GitHub's Primer**, with independently proposed tokens, component geometry, and a local reference implementation. Carbon and Primer retain their own names and authorship; neither publishes or endorses this theme. Precision is not an extracted Tamir portfolio theme.

## Suitability

These are Atlas assessments, not measured usability results.

| Project type | Fit | Reason and adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent workspace | Strong | Explicit lifecycle, attention, connection, and command states make agent activity inspectable. Document authority and recovery in the project contract. |
| Operations dashboard | Strong | Aligned tables, stable summaries, readable timestamps, and neutral surfaces support repeated checks. Add freshness and data provenance. |
| Administration interface | Strong | Clear grouping, visible labels, and bounded primary actions suit configuration and record work. Define validation, permissions, and confirmation separately. |
| Developer tool | Strong | Sans interface text and short monospace identifiers provide technical precision without turning every paragraph into a log. |
| Review queue | Strong | Persistent selection and an explicit path from list to evidence support comparison and deliberate decisions. Include keyboard and focus behavior. |
| Data visualization workspace | Conditional | The base supports surrounding controls and tables; a project still needs its own chart scales, legends, accessible alternatives, and update rules. |
| Portfolio or expressive campaign | Conditional | Technical presentation may fit engineering work; projects requiring imagery, expressive branding, or long narrative need deliberate adaptations. |

The theme provides a visual and interaction starting point. It does not authorize execution, decide approval policy, or define backend reliability. Load relevant [Agent Experience guidance](../../knowledge/agent-experience.md) when preparing those decisions.

Precision is an original Atlas synthesis informed by Carbon and Primer. Every palette value, type size, radius, density choice, layout option, and interaction contract below is an **Atlas proposal**, unless explicitly marked **reference observation**. **Reference observation:** Carbon assigns colors by role and uses neutral layers to organize regions. Precision applies that concept to a separate cool palette; these values are not Carbon or Primer tokens.

Use page as the base, panel for the main working region, and surface for a supporting region. Dark layers become lighter. Apply grouping only where it clarifies the task: a page of nested cards adds unnecessary boundaries. Reserve action color for controls, selected context, and deliberate emphasis. Keep prose links underlined.

Muted text is readable supporting information. Decorative dividers do not meet the necessary-boundary target; use control border where a boundary identifies an input or control. Selection supports an explicit selected state, along with a non-color marker and applicable semantics.

Semantic foregrounds are calculated on page, panel, and surface, not on invented colored badge fills. Accompany each status with text and, when useful, a recognizable icon. “Running,” “Needs review,” “Connection lost,” and “Cancellation requested” describe different dimensions; do not collapse them into a single colored dot. A blue action is not a statement of safety or permission.

## Typography and hierarchy

**Reference observation:** Carbon uses IBM Plex and distinguishes productive and expressive type sets. Precision selects IBM Plex Sans for interface and reading text, with IBM Plex Mono for short technical values. The sizes below are Atlas choices, not a complete Carbon token transcription.

| Role | Proposed family and weight | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intro heading | IBM Plex Sans 600 | `clamp(1.75rem, 3vw, 2.5rem)` | `1.15` |
| Page heading | IBM Plex Sans 600 | `2rem` | `1.2` |
| Section heading | IBM Plex Sans 600 | `1.75rem` | `1.25` |
| Detail heading | IBM Plex Sans 600 | `1.5rem` | `1.3` |
| Body or extended reading | IBM Plex Sans 400 | `1rem` | `1.6` |
| Labels, table values, short metadata | IBM Plex Sans 400/600 | `0.875rem` | `1.5` |
| Code, run ID, short command | IBM Plex Mono 400 | `0.875rem` | `1.5` |

Use normal tracking for body and control text; brief headings may use `-0.015em`. Keep headings in sentence case and reserve uppercase for short, optional indexes. Large marketing display typography is a project adaptation, not the operational default. A page has one primary heading and continuous semantic levels.

Limit reading passages to about 65 characters per line. Use tabular numerals for comparable numeric columns and timestamps. Monospace identifiers must wrap or have a clearly contained code region; they must not widen the whole page. Do not truncate essential state, errors, or action meaning behind a hover-only tooltip.

The preview names IBM Plex but ships no fonts. Validate actual package weights, script coverage, fallback, wrapping, and rhythm in each project. Different Plex script packages have separate contributors and version records; a family name does not establish every glyph's availability.

## Spacing, density, and layout

**Reference observation:** Carbon's 2x Grid begins with an 8px mini unit. Precision uses an Atlas scale of 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, and 64px; 4 and 12px are deliberate refinements, not a claim that the full scale is Carbon's grid.

- Default compact panels use 16px padding and 14px short metadata; extended reading remains 16px.
- Comfortable adaptation uses 24px panel padding and 16px specimen text.
- Label to control: 8px. Related controls: 12–16px. Separate working regions: 24–32px.
- Keep action areas at least 44px in both densities; dense content does not require small targets.
- Proposed content maximum: 1280px; gutters start at 16px and grow to 24px when space permits.

**Reference observation:** Primer identifies header, content, and supporting pane regions and describes list-detail layouts. Precision proposes a compact workspace header, a run list, an inline detail region, and secondary evidence beneath it. The preview's composition and breakpoint choices are original Atlas work.

Use shared starting edges for titles, labels, data, and actions. Add a supporting pane only if the content benefits from remaining visible. Begin with one column and add columns when both list and detail retain readable widths. Do not blend Carbon's grid breakpoints with Primer's column counts as if they were one upstream rule; record the project's actual content-fit decisions.

On narrow screens, place the list before detail in the same logical DOM order, provide an explicit return action, and preserve selection and filters. Avoid a large navigation stack that pushes the task out of view. Wide semantic tables may scroll inside a labeled keyboard-focusable region; general page content must reflow. Wrap long values and test translated labels before selecting a breakpoint.

## Geometry and elevation

Proposed panel and control radius: **4px**. Resting shadows: **none**. Use one-pixel decorative rules, stronger necessary control boundaries, flat layers, and explicit space. The geometry is an Atlas choice; it is not a claim about Carbon's component corners or Primer's radius tokens.

An optional anchored popover or dialog may use limited elevation after composited contrast and focus checks. The reference preview does not require floating overlays. Keep data and action surfaces opaque; gradients, glow, glass, moving grids, and cursor effects do not define this theme. [Effects.md](effects.md) documents selection criteria and limits.

## Component behavior

| Component | Proposed rule |
| --- | --- |
| Primary action | Verified action/on-action pair, stable dimensions, meaningful verb, 4px radius, visible focus, and brief feedback. |
| Secondary action | Neutral background with readable text; necessary border remains visible. |
| Navigation | Explicit current location and clear destination; appearance follows applicable `aria-current` or selected semantics. |
| Filter | Visible label, native control, immediate useful results, preserved selected-item context, and clear empty-result recovery. |
| Run list | Persistent run IDs and textual states; inspection is an explicit action rather than an unlabeled clickable row. |
| Detail | Meaningful heading, evidence, confirmed state, separate pending command, and an explicit return path. |
| Input | Visible associated label, panel background, control border, help linked to the control, and nearby error recovery. |
| Status | Text plus optional icon on verified neutral surfaces; explain freshness and command acknowledgement. |
| Table | Semantic headers and caption/context, comparable numeric alignment, contained wide content, no fake live data. |
| Disclosure | Native details/summary for optional evidence, visible expanded state, and no motion dependency. |
| Dialog | Accessible name, bounded content, deliberate focus entry/return, reachable dismissal and action; project-specific implementation required. |

Define default, hover, focus, pressed/selected, unavailable, and pending states as appropriate. Keep explanatory text legible even when its adjacent control is disabled. A control disabled by permissions needs a visible explanation when users need to understand the limitation. Error messages describe the problem and next action.

## Agent and operations interaction contract

**Reference observation:** Primer's Copilot guidance calls for visible focus, focus continuity, accessible state, and announcements of asynchronous work and errors. The contract below is Precision's explicit Atlas proposal, informed by that guidance and the shared [Agent Experience guide](../../knowledge/agent-experience.md).

1. Keep confirmed execution, user attention, connection, and pending command separate. Preserve the last confirmed execution when a connection disappears; mark the information stale and offer recovery.
2. A deliberate “Inspect” action opens evidence and focuses its detail heading. This is a navigation choice. Selection used for rapid in-place browsing may instead retain focus in the list; a project must choose and document one behavior.
3. Returning to the list preserves selected context and restores the originating control when visible. If a filter hides it, preserve the filter and detail and focus the search control with an explanation.
4. Requesting cancellation sets **Cancellation requested**; confirmed execution stays **Running** until an acknowledgement arrives. Do not silently equate a sent command with a confirmed outcome.
5. Announce meaningful changes in a polite status region. Avoid announcing every stream token or repeatedly moving focus on background updates. User-invoked navigation may transfer focus; asynchronous status changes normally do not.
6. State the acting agent, scope, available evidence, and effect before consequential actions. A project must separately define authority, approval, retry, recovery, audit records, and backend idempotency.

The reference preview uses fictional local records and manual simulation controls. It sends no agent command or network request. Its cancellation and connection transitions demonstrate wording and context, not production synchronization.

## Appearance and accessibility

Support light, dark, and system appearance. Apply a saved choice before paint where possible, respond to live system changes when system is selected, and preserve usable defaults if storage or initialization fails.

Proposed focus: **3px** solid focus-color outline with **3px** offset, outside the target on a neutral surface. These dimensions are Atlas choices. Inspect actual adjacent surfaces and clipping; use system `Highlight` under forced colors. Never remove the ring without an equally usable replacement.

Use native landmarks and controls, a useful skip link, visible labels, logical keyboard order, and context-preserving focus. A 44px area is an Atlas comfort target, not a claim that it is WCAG's minimum. Test narrow reflow, 200% text resizing, native zoom, keyboard interaction, screen-reader information, and actual rendered contrast in each project.

Essential information remains present without animation or JavaScript. [Motion rules](motion.md) make feedback immediate under reduced motion and motion-off. Preserve explicit pending, failure, and stale information in all fallbacks; a spinner cannot carry the only status meaning.

# Precision — optional effects

Precision's identity comes from structured layers, aligned information, modest typography, stable controls, and explicit states. Decorative effects are optional project selections. [Design rules](design.md) define the readable content layer; [motion rules](motion.md) define immediate fallbacks.

## Structured surface layers

**Reference concept:** Carbon uses role-based neutral layers to organize depth. **Atlas proposal:** use the Precision page/panel/surface values to distinguish a main work region from related evidence. Keep the layers opaque and flat. Separate regions with spacing, headings, and useful rules before adding another container.

This is ordinary static styling. It requires no animation or component runtime. The colors and geometry are independent Atlas choices, not a reproduction of IBM's theme values.

## Optional overlay elevation

An anchored menu, popover, or dialog may use one restrained shadow and a visible boundary when it must appear above the working surface. Select exact values in the project design document and inspect both appearances. This theme does not prescribe an untested universal shadow token.

Keep the overlay within the viewport, maintain a clear dismissal path, and ensure focus is not clipped. Use the correct native or accessible interaction behavior; a shadow does not define modality. Under forced colors, retain a visible system-color boundary. No floating overlay is selected in the reference preview.

## Selection and state emphasis

Use a bounded selected background, an explicit marker, and applicable semantics to keep the chosen item identifiable. A status may use a small icon or rule with its text label. Keep the necessary meaning present when color, JavaScript, or visual decoration is unavailable.

AI origin or provenance may have a plain textual label when users need it to interpret evidence. A project should decide the label's wording, scope, and source record. Precision requires no AI glow, gradient, animated emblem, or decorative attribution badge.

Do not pulse “Running,” move rows during filtering, or decorate an unacknowledged command as complete. A confirmed outcome may receive brief static emphasis; keep a persistent readable record. Fake charts, quantified progress, and decorative telemetry are not substitutes for measured data.

## Acceptance checks

Verify actual text and boundary contrast, selected-state meaning, focus visibility, forced-color fallback, narrow reflow, keyboard use, and uninterrupted text selection. Decoration must not intercept pointer events, change reading order, hide evidence, or require motion to communicate status. No canvas, custom cursor, or continuous effect is included.

[Sources.md](sources.md) records upstream concept credits and the original Atlas implementation boundary. An added effect or imported package needs its own creator, version, license, and focused validation record.

# Precision — motion specification

Motion supports repeated work through brief feedback while preserving targets and context. Precision includes no automatic entrance sequence, scrolling animation, animated cursor, moving artwork, row reordering, or continuous loop.

## Referenced source settings

**IBM Carbon reference:** productive motion is subdued task feedback; expressive motion serves occasional emphasis. Its documented productive standard easing is `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0.38, 0.9)`. The documented duration tokens include 110ms (`duration-fast-02`) and 150ms (`duration-moderate-01`). [Source credits](sources.md) identify the responsible IBM team and accessed reference.

These are selected reference facts, not an imported Carbon runtime or a transcription of its complete motion system. Precision chooses where to apply them.

## Proposed project rules

| Role | Atlas choice | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Control color and border feedback | 110ms with the referenced productive standard curve | Keep position and dimensions stable. The reference preview selects this treatment. |
| Optional small secondary disclosure | Up to 150ms with the same curve | Only if a project deliberately selects motion; reveal useful content promptly and keep focus stable. The preview's native disclosures are immediate. |
| Filtering, selection, status, and appearance | Immediate state/content changes | Do not use a duration as an artificial processing delay. |
| User-invoked detail navigation | Immediate content and deliberate focus transfer | Do not fade essential evidence in from an invisible initial state. |
| Background updates | Preserve current position and focus | Announce meaningful changes without stealing focus or shifting the active item. |

Any different distance, overlay, or expressive event needs a project-specific decision and check. A short timing does not justify moving a repeatedly used target. Keep initial page content visible immediately, including when script initialization is unavailable.

## Reduced motion and user control

Honor `prefers-reduced-motion` from first paint. OS reduced motion overrides an enabled motion preference. A visible motion choice may disable brief feedback without changing available information or controls.

- Make transitions immediate under reduced motion or motion-off.
- Remove transforms and entrance offsets; render final content visible.
- Keep navigation scrolling immediate.
- Preserve pending commands, stale data explanations, outcomes, and state announcements without animation.
- Do not replace a stopped effect with hidden content or an indefinite blank state.

Test live OS preference changes, saved motion preference, keyboard focus, immediate initial content, and useful no-JavaScript behavior. The reference preview's checks cover its implemented feedback only; they do not validate unimplemented overlay or disclosure animation.

# Pulse

Condensed headings, lime against ink, angled poster geometry, and generous spacing give Pulse a campaign character. Short display text carries emphasis; ordinary-width body text, stable controls, and readable schedules carry the work. Its identity is designed dark-first, with a complete light adaptation and a System appearance choice.

Pulse is an **original Interface Atlas synthesis**, developed for **Tamir (Phi Vuong Tuong Tam) with Codex AI assistance**. It studies modular CSS-token and adaptive-preference concepts from **Adam Argyle and Open Props contributors**, with additional animation-performance guidance by **Kayce Basques and Rachel Andrew**. Every palette, typography, layout, geometry, and timing value here is an Atlas proposal. Pulse is not a portfolio extraction or an official Open Props theme.

## Suitability

These are Atlas assessments, not measured usability results.

| Project type | Fit | Reason and adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Creative event | Strong | Poster emphasis and explicit program details suit a design gathering or exhibition. Keep real dates, venue, access information, and registration terms accurate. |
| Campaign site | Strong | One clear headline and a bounded accent can support a focused message. Preserve readable claims and a clear action without requiring motion to understand it. |
| Launch page | Strong | Bold short type can introduce a new offering. Product capabilities, availability, pricing, and evidence still need the project's own truth checks. |
| Community program | Strong | Session collections and a local selection model help explain a program. Add actual participation, access, privacy, and moderation behavior when needed. |
| Schedule planner | Conditional | The preview demonstrates choosing fixed sessions, reviewing overlaps, and recovering locally. Real scheduling needs timezone, travel, capacity, persistence, and service rules. |
| Long-form publication | Conditional | Retain comfortable body type and a bounded measure; reserve condensed display and angled geometry for short emphasis. |
| Agent or operations workspace | Conditional | Tone down poster prominence for repeated work and define authority, execution, pending commands, freshness, errors, and recovery independently. |

Choose the adaptation for actual tasks and content. A bright theme does not establish urgency, confidence, attendance, execution, or success. Use relevant [Agent Experience guidance](../../knowledge/agent-experience.md) when preparing an agent interface.

## Package

- [Design specification](design.md): proposed palette, typography, hierarchy, spacing, geometry, components, planner states, and numerical limits.
- [Motion specification](motion.md): brief feedback, a deliberately activated finite study, and immediate static alternatives.
- [Optional effects](effects.md): original poster geometry and the separate decorative motion study.
- [Sources and credits](sources.md): reference roles, pinned Open Props evidence, font creators, reuse terms, and Atlas proposals.

No theme-specific framework, token library, component package, or animation runtime is required.

## Preview and validation

The **[live Pulse reference preview](https://tamir39.github.io/interface-atlas/themes/pulse/preview/)** presents an original fictional design gathering, component specimens, six sample sessions, and a local plan/review flow. The [preview notes](preview/README.md) describe its behavior; [index.html](preview/index.html) also opens offline without a build. Original HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and vector geometry include local font fallbacks and no imported Open Props implementation. Local-only body-face aliases preserve ordinary-width text when exact Barlow faces are installed; otherwise the body uses Segoe UI/sans-serif. No font file is distributed or downloaded.

The preview defaults to **System** appearance. Its hero poster retains a dark composition in both appearances; that bounded preview choice does not force the rest of a light page into dark appearance. Essential content and planning remain available independently of the optional motion study.

Read the [validation report](validation.md) for actual browser evidence and its limits. [Design.md](design.md) records separate opaque numerical color calculations. Status remains **draft**: representative checks do not establish production readiness, intended named-font rendering, complete accessibility, assistive technology behavior, real event booking, or calendar integration.
