Use page as the base, panel for a useful grouping, and tints selectively. Alignment, spacing, and headings can establish structure without putting every region in a panel. Keep the strong dark lime limited to deliberate emphasis and actions. The light adaptation uses a darker action green for readable ordinary text and explicit filled actions.

Use action/on-action and hover/on-action as defined pairs. An accent mark is not automatically interactive. Decorative dividers and poster shapes do not identify a usable control; apply the necessary border where a boundary communicates interaction. Do not use a faint divider to outline the only sign of a text field.

Warning, danger, and information are **foreground roles** on the six page/panel/surface/tint backgrounds. They do not define filled status colors. Pair every status with readable text. Filled success and note treatments use their own on-success/on-note foregrounds. A selected session is not a success or confirmed booking.

On selected surfaces, use **ink labels, ink markers, underlined ink links, and ink boundaries where required**. The proposed dark necessary border is below 3:1 against selected surface. Using ink consistently in both appearances avoids propagating that weak pairing. Keep a visible selected label or marker in addition to the background. The proposed browser text selection uses selected surface with ink.

The reference hero retains the **dark poster palette in both page appearances**. Its local foregrounds, links, boundaries, and focus indicators must use the corresponding dark pairings; the surrounding page still follows the user's appearance. This is a preview composition choice rather than a universal requirement for every project header.

## Typography and hierarchy

**Proposed display family:** Barlow Condensed, 600/700. **Proposed body/control family:** Barlow, 400/500/600. Both are credited to **Jeremy Tribby**; font-package notices and additional contributor roles are in [sources.md](sources.md).

| Role | Family / weight | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Display | Barlow Condensed 700 | `clamp(3.5rem, 10vw, 8rem)` | `0.95` |
| Page heading | Barlow Condensed 600–700 | `clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 4.5rem)` | `1.05` |
| Section heading | Barlow Condensed 600 | `clamp(2rem, 4vw, 3rem)` | `1.1` |
| Card heading | Barlow 600 | `1.25rem` | `1.3` |
| Introduction | Barlow 400 | `1.125rem` | `1.6` |
| Body / reading | Barlow 400 | `1rem` | `1.6` |
| Labels / supporting text | Barlow 400–600 | `0.875rem` | `1.5` |
| Text-entry controls | Barlow 400 | `1rem` | `1.5` |
| Short technical sample | Local Consolas / monospace | `0.875rem` | Inherited readable line height |

Keep display tracking mild at **`-0.015em`** and ordinary body/control tracking normal. Reserve uppercase and condensed display for short headings, not paragraphs, error explanations, or schedule details. Do not horizontally scale text to simulate a condensed font. Recheck unusually long headings and use explicit line breaks only when they preserve meaning across widths and languages.

Use a continuous semantic heading hierarchy. A visually large word still needs the appropriate document role. Proposed reading measure is **65ch**, checked with the actual selected font. Use tabular numerals where times align or values change; do not obscure time ranges behind abbreviations.

The preview ships no font files and makes no remote font requests. It names Barlow Condensed with local Impact/Arial Narrow/sans-serif fallbacks. Body text uses the local-only CSS alias **`Pulse Barlow Local`**, then Segoe UI/sans-serif. Three normal-style `@font-face` declarations match explicit local face names: **Barlow Regular / Barlow-Regular** for 400, **Barlow Medium / Barlow-Medium** for 500, and **Barlow SemiBold / Barlow-SemiBold** for 600. Their sources use only `local()`, with no `url()`. This avoids the inspected Windows family-name collision in which plain `Barlow` resolved to Barlow Condensed. The body remains ordinary width, falling back when those exact installed faces are unavailable. Different local faces have different metrics and weights; intended named-font rendering, language coverage, and final rhythm remain project checks. Text-entry controls retain at least **16px** text in the mobile adaptation.

**Reference implementation adaptations:** the preview uses a tighter `0.9` poster-display line height, retains the display's `-0.015em` tracking, and changes its display clamp to `clamp(3.5rem, 10vw, 6rem)` at 52rem and `clamp(3.5rem, 17vw, 6rem)` at 38rem after the artwork stacks. Its theme-page title uses `clamp(3rem, 6vw, 5rem)`, section headings use `clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 4.5rem)`, and ordinary card headings are `1.375rem`. Labels are 14px; short tags/captions are generally 12px, with the artwork caption 10px in the intermediate layout and 12px again when stacked. These are bounded preview choices rather than new universal theme defaults; resizing, wrapping, fallback metrics, and actual readability remain project checks.

## Spacing and layout

**Proposed scale:** 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, and 96px.

- Label to control: 8px; related controls: 12px.
- Related content: 16–24px; major sections: 48–96px.
- Comfortable panel inset: 24px; compact specimen inset: 16px.
- Typical content maximum: 1120px; reading maximum: 65ch.
- Proposed gutters: 24px on small screens and 40px when room permits; adapt at the narrowest content widths.

Start with one column and add columns only when actual content fits. Keep logical DOM order, then use alignment and bounded artwork to establish a poster composition. Avoid relying on rotated text, unusual spatial order, or a moving marquee to convey the program.

The preview's gathering and planner stay comfortable. Compact changes **only the neutral component specimen's inset from 24px to 16px**. Typography, action targets, geometry, schedule, review content, and poster retain their values. A project choosing broader density changes records them explicitly.

Session summaries need their full title, time range, and track. Keep useful metadata beside the corresponding action. A plan remains inspectable even if filters hide some of its sessions. Preserve selected sessions across filters and appearance changes; filtering does not silently discard a choice.

Where a semantic table genuinely requires horizontal room, contain overflow in a labeled keyboard-accessible scrolling region. The whole page must still reflow. Preserve long values, Vietnamese content, normal text selection, and enlarged text without clipping essential information.

The preview uses a **1240px** content maximum, 24px outer gutters normally, and 16px gutters at its narrow layout. Session/plan panels use 24px inset normally and 20px in the narrow layout; the preview preference panel also uses its own 20px inset. These content-fit adaptations remain separate from the specimen-only density switch. Program and planner collapse by content fit; their visual columns do not change the session collection's reading order.

## Geometry and elevation

**Proposed panels:** 12px corners. **Proposed controls:** 6px corners. Task surfaces rest flat; contrast, grouping, and spacing provide structure. Use an ink boundary where a selected state needs one rather than adding a glow or a moving outline.

Angled wedges, split circles, radial bars, and oversized cropped shapes may form bounded original poster artwork. They are decoration, not form controls or evidence of progress. Crop artwork inside its region without clipping focus rings, headings, or page overflow. Keep actionable content stable and unrotated. [Effects.md](effects.md) describes the optional study separately.

## Components and local planning behavior

| Component | Proposed rule |
| --- | --- |
| Primary action | Action/on-action, stable dimensions, hover action pair, and clear focus. |
| Secondary action | Ink text and a necessary border where its shape conveys interaction. |
| Prose link | Persistent underline or equivalent non-color cue; selected-surface links use ink. |
| Input / select | Visible associated label, readable value, neutral surface, and necessary boundary. |
| Session selection | Native button with a stable Add-to-plan label and `aria-pressed`; persistent selected text/marker. |
| Plan list | Explicit selected sessions and readable time ranges; removing a session restores a deliberate surviving focus target. |
| Review result | Explain empty-plan and overlapping-time conditions in text, with explicit recovery. A valid local result is a local check. |
| Status feedback | Polite concise announcement for ordinary changes; persistent readable errors/results rather than color alone. |
| Supporting content | Native `details`/`summary` where disclosure suits the content. |
| Decorative study | Explicit native activation, finite motion only when permitted, and a static equivalent. |

Define default, hover, focus, pressed/selected, unavailable, pending, and error states where relevant to the actual product. Do not add fictional loading, inventory pressure, or asynchronous booking to decorate this reference.

The preview has **six fixed fictional sessions** and an in-memory local plan. Selection and review are separate. Review checks the chosen sample time ranges for overlaps; changing a selection invalidates a previous review rather than continuing to present it as current. Explain both overlapping sessions and provide a route to change the choice. Removing one item, clearing the plan, or hiding a selected session with filters must not strand focus or silently change unrelated preferences.

The planner is not a booking, payment, calendar, attendance, capacity, or agent-execution service. It makes no network request and reserves nothing. Real scheduling needs an explicit timezone/day model, server validation, accessibility requirements, availability, travel time, persistence, permissions, and truthful pending/confirmed/error states. Do not infer those capabilities from a green local review result.

## Appearance and accessibility

Support **Light, Dark, and System**. The preview starts with System and follows live OS appearance; dark-first identity does not override an explicit preference. Apply valid saved settings before paint where possible. Malformed, unavailable, or blocked storage preserves usable defaults. Only appearance, specimen density, and motion preference persist; the local plan resets on reload.

**Proposed focus:** 3px ink outline with 5px offset; forced colors uses `Highlight`. Verify adjacent backgrounds and prevent clipping, including on the fixed dark poster and selected sessions. Listed token pairs do not establish complete focus conformance.

Use native controls, landmarks, descriptive headings, a useful skip link, and logical keyboard order. The comfortable target proposal is **44px**, a usability target rather than a statement of WCAG's minimum. Verify activation, pressed states, review/focus recovery, announcements, text resizing, reflow, and rendered contrast. Without JavaScript, session information remains readable and controls requiring runtime behavior stay unavailable with an explanation.

Essential content, planning, review, and error recovery happen immediately and independently of animation completion. Follow [motion.md](motion.md) for reduced/off/hidden cancellation and static alternatives. [Preview notes](preview/README.md) record the actual local behavior.

# Pulse — optional effects

Pulse's core identity comes from condensed short headings, lime/ink contrast, and deliberate spacing. Projects choose optional decoration separately from functional design. **All treatments here are original Atlas proposals.** No third-party effect implementation, Open Props stylesheet, or portfolio renderer is imported. [Sources](sources.md) records conceptual references and creator roles.

## Bounded poster geometry

Use a static, original composition of bars, wedges, split circles, or cropped geometric forms in a bounded hero or campaign region. Keep ordinary navigation and body text in HTML with a stable reading order. A poster may use the dark palette inside a light page when its own foreground, action, focus, and boundary pairs are defined deliberately.

- Mark pure decoration `aria-hidden` and prevent it receiving pointer input or keyboard focus.
- Crop artwork inside its own region; avoid whole-page horizontal overflow and never clip headings or focus rings.
- Keep text, actionable targets, and session information unrotated. Use angle and overlap in the artwork rather than forcing users to read tilted paragraphs.
- Preserve the composition as a static illustration on reduced-motion, motion-off, unsupported-animation, and no-JavaScript paths.
- A bright shape or bar conveys no progress, availability, booking state, attendance, agent activity, or urgency.

The preview's original dark poster and static vector geometry are Atlas compositions. It uses no external illustration, icon package, canvas renderer, shader, cursor effect, or brand asset.

## Optional motion study

The preview includes one separate **Play motion study** action. It requests a finite **600ms** movement of three decorative bars using transform/opacity. Static geometry is present before activation; no content waits for the study. The bars return to their normal final composition and never loop.

Open Props informs user-preference gating, and the article by **Kayce Basques and Rachel Andrew** informs animation-property selection. The geometry, timing, activation, and lifecycle are Atlas choices; no example code is reused. Keep actual rendering performance and interaction accessibility as project checks rather than treating a property name as proof.

Follow [motion.md](motion.md): cancel existing movement on repeat activation, motion-off, reduced motion, and a hidden document. Do not replay after visibility or appearance changes. An unavailable animation API keeps the static equivalent. The study does not alter or approve a plan and has no backend effect.

## Task-surface restraint

The planner uses flat surfaces with 12px corners, controls with 6px corners, and readable necessary boundaries. Selection uses persistent labels/markers and ink where needed. Avoid glowing selection rings, reactive backgrounds under schedule text, moving button targets, or repeated hover lifts in a review task.

Keep the native pointer and normal text selection. Faint decorative dividers cannot substitute for input boundaries, error text, or focus indicators. No optional effect expands the scope of the preview's [validation evidence](validation.md).

# Pulse — motion specification

Motion is optional expression around immediate content and stable tasks. **Every duration, curve, property choice, and lifecycle rule here is an Atlas proposal.** [Source credits](sources.md) identify the conceptual Open Props and web.dev references without assigning them authorship of Pulse's motion.

## Feedback and finite study

| Role | Proposed setting | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Component feedback | **150ms**, `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | Brief color/border feedback; not a simulated booking or processing delay. |
| Decorative study | **600ms**, finite transform/opacity movement | Explicit activation of one bounded three-bar composition. No autoplay or loop. |
| Selection, filtering, review, errors, and focus | Immediate | No dependency on an animation finishing. |
| Reduced motion or motion off | Immediate static final state | OS reduced motion takes priority over the enabled project preference. |

Short hover feedback may paint a small region; it is not claimed to run only on the compositor. The separate decorative study uses transform/opacity and leaves layout dimensions and controls stable. The web.dev reference informs property selection and deliberate performance inspection; it does not guarantee smoothness on every device. Do not add permanent `will-change` without an observed need.

The original poster is visible from first paint. There is no entrance sequence, stagger, marquee, cursor follower, animated scrolling, flashing emphasis, or continuous background. Adding a session does not bounce its card or move the focused control. A successful local review uses persistent text, not a celebratory animation standing in for an outcome.

## Deliberate decorative activation

The preview's **Play motion study** button requests one 600ms run on three decorative bars. It does not start an event, submit a plan, invoke an agent, or advance the planner.

- Do not autoplay on load, scrolling, hover, appearance changes, filtering, selection, or review.
- A repeat activation cancels the prior run before requesting its replacement; animation instances do not accumulate.
- Keep the static final composition present when idle and restore it after completion or cancellation.
- Motion off, a live reduced-motion preference, or a hidden document cancels active movement immediately. Becoming visible again does not automatically replay it.
- If the animation API is unavailable, keep the static composition and explain the unavailable study without blocking other controls.
- Keep decoration outside the accessibility tree and pointer/keyboard hit testing. The native study button keeps a stable position and focus.

This is a selected optional demonstration. Projects may omit it entirely and retain Pulse's identity through color, type, and static geometry. A future project choosing additional motion documents its purpose, activation, cancellation, and static equivalent.

## Reduced motion and user control

Honor `prefers-reduced-motion` from the first render. A visible motion checkbox lets users make feedback immediate even when the OS permits movement. Turning motion on does not override OS reduced motion or automatically start the study.

Keep essential headings, session information, plan entries, review/error content, and recovery links visible without motion. Focus transfers and status announcements remain immediate. No state should depend on motion alone; use stable labels and readable results.

Test the initial static view, one finite run, repeat activation, live reduced/off changes, document visibility cancellation, unsupported API behavior, and no-JavaScript content. Representative browser checks do not establish actual low-end-device frame performance or validate unimplemented future effects. [Validation.md](validation.md) records the evidence actually collected.

# Swiss

Confident sans-serif typography, shared alignment, paper and charcoal surfaces, precise rules, and a restrained red accent make content easy to scan. Flat panels and nearly square controls keep geometry direct. Short feedback supports deliberate interaction without introducing continuous motion.

This entry adapts the Swiss direction in **Tamir (Phi Vuong Tuong Tam)'s portfolio**, retaining observed values and distinguishing them from portable Atlas proposals. Its primary typeface is Manrope; JetBrains Mono has a small technical role. Swiss design history informs further study, but historical designers are not credited as authors of Tamir's implementation.

## Suitability

These are Atlas assessments, not measured usability results.

| Project type | Fit | Reason and adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Portfolio or case studies | Strong | Large headings and an aligned project index make work and evidence prominent. Keep body text comfortably sized and readable. |
| Publication or journal | Strong | Consistent columns and clear type roles support stories and navigation. Use a bounded reading measure and responsive reading order. |
| Studio or architecture site | Strong | Precise geometry and restrained color work with project imagery, names, and concise descriptions. Each image requires its own provenance. |
| Documentation | Strong | Flat sections, visible rules, and explicit links support scanning. Add robust navigation and code conventions for the project's scale. |
| Agent workspace or review queue | Conditional | Align metadata and actions, preserve context, and use textual states. Compact spacing is a documented project adaptation. |
| Dense analytics | Conditional | Requires additional chart, data, density, and update rules. A bold hero does not define a usable monitoring interface. |

Choose the adaptation according to the project's content and tasks. The visual theme does not define agent authority, execution, approval, or recovery behavior; use relevant [Agent Experience guidance](../../knowledge/agent-experience.md) when preparing those decisions.

## Package

- [Design specification](design.md): color, typography, hierarchy, grid, geometry, components, appearance, and accessibility rules.
- [Motion specification](motion.md): observed feedback and entrance settings, portable proposals, and reduced-motion behavior.
- [Optional effects](effects.md): structural rules, optional kinetic grid, and precision-square cursor.
- [Sources and credits](sources.md): pinned source files, creator roles, conceptual references, font terms, and adaptation records.

No theme-specific framework or animation runtime is required.

Page is the base; surface supports secondary regions; panel groups content where a separate surface is useful. Prefer alignment and rules over a card around every element. Action and on-action form an explicit button pair. Reserve red emphasis for important actions and selected expressive details so it does not overwhelm hierarchy.

Muted text remains readable supporting text. Decorative dividers have insufficient contrast to serve as the sole necessary input boundary; use the proposed control border when a boundary identifies a control. An ornamental rule does not need to become a control boundary.

Warning, danger, and information are foreground colors on the verified page, surface, and panel backgrounds. They do not specify filled buttons or badges. Use a textual status and optional icon; color supplements meaning. A red action does not imply danger, and a destructive action needs explicit wording and its own verified state treatment.

Pair success with on-success for a filled success region, and note with on-note for a note. Selection indicates text selection or a selected item with explicit semantics. Recheck any different background, opacity, compositing, image, or blend.

## Typography and hierarchy

**Source families:** Manrope for body text, controls, and expressive Swiss headings; JetBrains Mono 400/500 for short code, indexes, and technical identifiers. The source globally also loads DM Serif Display for other themes; that does not make it a Swiss default.

The pinned source loads Latin and Vietnamese for Manrope and Latin for JetBrains Mono. Verify the actual selected package, language coverage, fallback, and weight availability for each project. The preview names these families but ships no font files.

**Source observation:** the portfolio's Swiss hero uses Manrope 800 with `-0.075em` tracking, and selected project titles use `-0.055em`. These are specific source selectors, not portable body or control typography. Atlas proposes milder display tracking and normal tracking in reading and interface text.

| Role | Proposed family and weight | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Display | Manrope 800 | `clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 6rem)` | `1.02` |
| Page heading | Manrope 700 | `clamp(2rem, 4vw, 3.5rem)` | `1.1` |
| Section heading | Manrope 700 | `1.5rem` | `1.25` |
| Card heading | Manrope 700 | `1.125rem` | `1.35` |
| Body | Manrope 400 | `1rem` | `1.6` |
| Introduction | Manrope 400 | `1.125rem` | `1.6` |
| Labels and supporting text | Manrope 400–600 | `0.875rem` | `1.5` |
| Code or short identifier | JetBrains Mono 400/500 | `0.875rem` | `1.5` |

Use display tracking around `-0.03em`; section and card headings may use up to `-0.02em`. Leave body and controls at normal tracking. Selected short indexes may be uppercase with modest positive tracking; do not set paragraphs or long labels in uppercase.

Make size and weight differences purposeful. A page has one primary heading and continuous semantic heading levels. Keep prose around 60–70 characters per line. Use tabular numerals for aligned counts, durations, and numeric columns. Monospace is a role, not a replacement for readable body text.

## Spacing and layout

**Proposed scale:** 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, and 96px.

- Label to control: 8px; related controls: 12–16px.
- Panel padding: 24px comfortable or 16px compact.
- Major sections: 48–96px according to reading and task density.
- Typical content maximum: 1200px; reading columns remain narrower.
- Gutters: 24px on small screens, 40px when space permits.

Align headings, prose, images, captions, and actions to shared starting edges. A proposed grid may use 12 columns on wide screens, 8 on medium screens, and 4 on small screens, with content spanning several columns. These counts are Atlas options, not a universal historical Swiss rule or a transcription of the source portfolio. The number of rendered columns and breakpoint values must follow actual content fit. Begin with a readable single column and add columns only when they help.

Asymmetric composition can balance a large heading with a narrow description or an index with wider detail. Preserve the same logical DOM order on every screen. Do not reorder a control visually away from the content it operates. Wrap long names and identifiers; contain a genuinely wide table in a labeled, keyboard-accessible scroll region instead of overflowing the whole page.

Compact density is a project adaptation: proposed body text 14px for short review metadata, 16px for extended reading, 16px panel padding, 12–16px related-group spacing, and at least 44px control areas. Keep the source 2px geometry and flat surfaces. Density changes must not remove labels, state explanations, or recovery actions.

## Geometry and elevation

**Source:** card radius 2px; control radius 2px; resting shadow `none` in both appearances. Source Swiss accents include 3–5px structural rules, flat panels, and an unrotated profile surface.

Keep panels and controls nearly square, with meaningful boundaries and visible spacing. Use a stronger rule sparingly to begin an important region. Small decorative rules do not substitute for headings or status labels. Avoid adding soft shadows, glass, bevels, and rounded capsules as incidental polish; document any deliberate departure in the project's design document.

The source's optional project hover translates horizontally and adds an offset accent edge. This is an interaction effect, distinct from its shadow-free resting geometry. It is not selected for the reference preview. See [effects.md](effects.md) and [motion.md](motion.md) for optional behavior and fallback.

## Component behavior

| Component | Proposed rule |
| --- | --- |
| Primary action | Action/on-action pair, action-hover feedback, 2px radius, stable dimensions, clear label, visible focus. |
| Secondary action | Panel or transparent surface, text foreground, stronger boundary where needed. |
| Prose link | Persistent underline or another explicit non-color cue; meaningful destination wording. |
| Navigation | Current location has textual or semantic identification plus a visible marker; selected color alone is insufficient. |
| Input | Visible associated label, panel background, text foreground, proposed control border, and nearby recovery information. |
| Content index | Shared title/metadata alignment; each destination has a distinct label and touch area. |
| Disclosure | Native summary and detail semantics, visible expanded state, reachable by keyboard. |
| Status | Text plus optional icon on a verified neutral surface; preserve separate lifecycle, attention, and connection meaning. |
| Table | Semantic headers, text aligned to the reading direction, numeric values aligned for comparison, contained overflow. |
| Dialog | Content-sized within the viewport; visible actions, accessible name, managed focus, and a clear dismissal path. |

Define default, hover, focus, pressed or selected, unavailable, and pending states where relevant. Pending copy such as “Saving…” explains what is happening without changing the control's position. Preserve existing information while updates arrive; a visual theme does not authorize backend commands.

Associate errors with fields, explain unavailable actions visibly when the reason matters, and keep recovery close to the problem. Do not hide essential text only in hover tooltips. For a review queue, record selected-item context, focus transfer, filtering behavior, and confirmation requirements in the project design document.

## Appearance and accessibility

Support light, dark, and system preferences. Apply a saved preference before paint where possible, follow live system changes when system is selected, and preserve essential content if storage or initialization fails.

**Source global focus:** 3px outline using text, offset 5px; forced colors uses `Highlight`. Leave enough space to prevent clipping and inspect contrast against adjacent surfaces.

Use native controls and landmarks, visible labels, a useful skip link, and logical keyboard order. A 44px touch area is an Atlas comfort target, not a claim about WCAG's minimum. Check reflow, text resizing, native browser zoom, keyboard use, screen-reader information, and actual AA contrast in each implemented project.

Essential content must remain visible without motion or JavaScript. Optional effects cannot block text selection, scrolling, focus, touch, or navigation. [Motion rules](motion.md) and [effect rules](effects.md) define immediate fallbacks.

# Swiss — optional effects

The theme's core identity comes from typography, alignment, flat geometry, and restrained color. A project explicitly selects any decorative effect. [Design rules](design.md) define the readable content layer; [motion rules](motion.md) define immediate fallbacks.

## Structural rules and static composition

**Source:** strong 3–5px rules introduce selected portfolio regions; resting surfaces have no shadow and 2px corners. This is ordinary styling, not an animation dependency.

**Atlas proposal:** use one deliberate rule to establish an important group, along with a semantic heading and useful spacing. A static grid study may appear in a hero if it remains separate from content, controls, and reading order. The reference preview's static composition is original Atlas artwork, not a Kinetic Grid implementation or exported historical poster.

## Kinetic grid

**Source concept:** Tamir's portfolio has an original Canvas 2D adaptation of a grid that bends near the pointer and responds to clicks with red ripples. Its notes credit **SatoriUI / @satoriui's [Kinetic Grid](https://21st.dev/@satoriui/components/kinetic-grid)**. The source describes custom interaction adaptations rather than imported catalog code.

The inspected component listing identifies SatoriUI and displays an MIT License label. Atlas includes none of that component's implementation. Before a future import, inspect the exact selected code package, copyright notice, and license text; a catalog label does not identify every dependency or replace required notices.

**Atlas proposal:** disabled by default. A project may select one bounded hero region and offer an explicit native control to enable motion. Avoid article reading, tables, logs, and frequently changing review workspaces.

- Keep all essential text, links, and controls in normal HTML and readable independently of artwork.
- Mark pure decoration `aria-hidden`; it must not intercept pointer input or keyboard navigation.
- Expose an intentional effect action through a separate native labeled button. Do not turn an unlabeled page background into an action.
- Use static composition for coarse pointers, touch, reduced motion, and motion-off.
- If adopting source performance behavior, defer desktop eligibility, cap pixel density at 2, and pause offscreen and in hidden tabs.
- Remove animation frames and resize, pointer, and visibility listeners when replacing or removing the effect.
- Recheck text and focus after compositing over every frame and background.

No canvas implementation is included in this theme package or its reference preview. Any implementation or authorized adaptation needs its own provenance and checks.

## Precision-square cursor

**Source character:** an optional 9px solid square supplementary to the native pointer, with the current theme color.

**Atlas proposal:** disabled by default. If selected for fine-pointer devices, keep the native pointer, prevent event interception, and hide the follower around text entry and keyboard interaction. Disable on coarse pointers, reduced motion, and motion-off; stop frames when settled. The square must not communicate selection, permission, progress, or availability.

The preview preserves the normal browser pointer and includes no follower.

## Optional project hover

**Source:** eligible portfolio cards may translate horizontally by 4px and add an offset red edge on hover. Shared press feedback may scale to `0.96`. These are observed interaction details, not resting elevation.

**Atlas proposal:** prefer color and border feedback. If a project selects movement, keep targets stable enough for repeated interaction, do not move focused controls, retain an equivalent focus treatment, and remove all transforms under reduced motion or motion-off. The reference preview does not select these movement effects.

## Acceptance checks

Verify composited contrast, focus visibility, native pointer behavior, keyboard access, text selection, touch fallback, explicit motion control, reduced motion, hidden/offscreen pausing, and cleanup. An effect failure must leave content and controls usable. A static fallback must not change meaning or reading order.

The source revision, creator, conceptual attribution, and reuse boundaries are recorded in [sources.md](sources.md).

# Swiss — motion specification

Short feedback should make interaction clear while keeping content and targets stable. These settings distinguish inspected source values from Atlas proposals. Pinned files and creator credits are recorded in [sources.md](sources.md).

## Retained source settings

| Role | Source setting | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSS component feedback | 160ms; declared `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | Source shorthand attaches theme easing explicitly to transform. Uniform easing for all feedback properties is an Atlas normalization. |
| Theme entrance | 180ms tween, `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` | Initial opacity 0 and horizontal offset -18px; final opacity 1 and offset 0. |
| Shared press feedback | Scale `0.96` | Optional source interaction; not mandatory for every control. |
| Eligible project hover | Horizontal translation 4px and offset accent edge | Optional portfolio movement, separate from flat resting geometry. |

The source helper defines the entrance, but the pinned artwork notes describe the homepage hero as immediately visible with no entrance or stagger after its separate brand introduction. Do not infer that every source region uses the entrance helper. Atlas does not adopt the portfolio loading introduction, animated identity sequence, theme reveal, or page-background theme cycling.

CSS feedback and entrance describe different roles. A single universal timing cannot represent both.

## Proposed project rules

Use 160ms color and border feedback with the declared CSS theme easing consistently as an Atlas normalization. The reference preview uses this restrained feedback only. Feedback duration is not a simulated loading delay.

Keep primary hero and page content visible immediately. If a project selects the source entrance, use it only for a secondary region once, keep essential information present, and avoid replaying when appearance changes, data refreshes, or the user returns. Avoid sequential letter reveals, typewriter text, and automatic staggering as default reading behavior.

For compact workflows, retain stable targets and immediate content. A project may choose 120–160ms feedback and an opacity-only panel change up to 180ms; record the chosen alternative. Do not animate sorting, filtering, streaming values, or pending commands by moving the focused item. Preserve selected context and provide meaningful status text.

The optional press scale and project hover may be omitted where they reduce pointer accuracy or repeated-use clarity. The preview omits movement, entrances, cursor effects, animated scrolling, and continuous loops.

## Reduced motion and user control

Honor `prefers-reduced-motion` from the first paint, with OS reduced motion taking precedence over an enabled project motion preference. A visible motion choice may turn off feedback animation without changing the information shown.

- Make transitions immediate under reduced motion or motion-off.
- Remove transforms and entrance offsets; render final content visible immediately.
- Keep navigation scroll behavior immediate.
- Replace optional canvas/cursor motion with static content; do not run hidden loops.
- Preserve state announcements and pending information without motion.

Test live preference changes, keyboard focus, immediate initial content, and fallback behavior without JavaScript. If a project adopts artwork, test its pause and cleanup separately; reference-preview checks do not validate unimplemented effects.
